questions.explain: MCSB is multicloud and is the default standard for Azure, AWS and GCP in Defender for Cloud, feeding Secure Score. Mappings show a feature helps meet a requirement, not full compliance. Defender for Cloud assesses MCSB natively.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure Resource Graph query that returns unhealthy Defender for Cloud recommendations (assessments).
questions.code:
securityresources
| where type == "____"
| where properties.status.code == "Unhealthy"
| project id, name = properties.displayName
options: microsoft.security/securescores
microsoft.security/assessments
microsoft.policyinsights/policystates
microsoft.security/alerts
questions.explain: Recommendations are stored as microsoft.security/assessments in securityresources, with a status code of Healthy, Unhealthy or NotApplicable. Secure scores are aggregate values, policy states live in policyresources, and alerts are threats, not posture assessments.

questions.case: Woodgrove's auditors require evidence of PCI DSS control status for its card platform in Azure. The CISO also wants engineers to keep a consistent cloud security baseline for all other workloads and to track improvement over time with one score.
questions.stem: What should the architect recommend in Defender for Cloud?
options: Remove MCSB and assign only PCI DSS to all subscriptions
Use Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager only and stop using Defender for Cloud
Assign PCI DSS as a custom Azure Policy initiative and disable the regulatory compliance dashboard
Keep MCSB as the baseline and add PCI DSS as an additional standard on the card platform subscriptions
questions.explain: MCSB stays as the universal baseline driving Secure Score, while PCI DSS is added where needed and tracked in the regulatory compliance dashboard. Removing MCSB loses the baseline; disabling the dashboard removes audit evidence; Compliance Manager alone doesn't give the Azure workload posture view.

questions.stem: Which solution detects that a departing employee downloaded large volumes of confidential files shortly after their resignation was recorded in the HR system?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
questions.explain: Insider Risk Management's 'data theft by departing users' template uses an HR connector plus activity signals. ID Protection assesses sign-in and user compromise risk, Defender for Identity detects on-premises AD attacks, and Communication Compliance reviews messages.

questions.stem: A managed service provider (MSP) currently has permanent Global Administrator rights in your tenant through legacy delegated admin. You need to reduce supply chain risk from the MSP while keeping its support access. What should you implement?
options: Granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) with least-privilege, time-bound roles
Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect with Teams shared channels
Cross-tenant synchronization of the MSP's users into your tenant
Self-service password reset for the MSP's accounts
questions.explain: GDAP replaces broad delegated admin with specific, time-limited roles for partners. B2B direct connect is for Teams shared channels, cross-tenant sync is for multi-tenant organisations, and SSPR doesn't reduce partner privilege.

questions.case: Contoso builds its customer portal with GitHub Actions and many open-source npm packages. A recent industry incident involved a malicious package update that stole cloud credentials from build pipelines. Contoso's pipelines authenticate to Azure with a client secret stored as a repository secret.
questions.stem: Which THREE controls BEST reduce Contoso's supply chain risk? Select THREE.
options: Enable Dependabot alerts and maintain an SBOM for the portal
Replace the client secret with workload identity federation (OIDC) for the pipeline
Enable Azure DDoS Network Protection on the portal's virtual network
Restrict the pipeline identity to the minimum RBAC scope it needs
Move the portal to a different Azure region
questions.explain: Dependency monitoring and an SBOM find malicious or vulnerable packages; OIDC federation removes a long-lived secret that could be stolen; least privilege limits damage if the pipeline is abused. DDoS protection and region changes don't address supply chain compromise.

questions.stem: For each statement about protecting against insider, external and supply chain attacks, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Purview Insider Risk Management shows pseudonymised user names by default to protect privacy.
A perimeter firewall is the primary defence against a compromised software update from a trusted vendor.
Access reviews of guest and partner accounts help limit third-party access risk.

questions.explain: Insider Risk Management pseudonymises users by default. A trusted vendor update passes through the perimeter, so you need dependency, integrity and least-privilege controls instead. Access reviews remove stale partner access.

questions.stem: Which MCSB AI security control requires that only models passing a formal verification and approval process are deployed to production?
options: AI-3: Adopt safety meta-prompts
AI-1: Ensure use of approved models
AI-5: Ensure human-in-the-loop
AI-7: Perform continuous AI red teaming
questions.explain: AI-1 addresses model provenance and approval. AI-3 is about system prompts that steer behaviour, AI-5 requires human approval of critical actions, and AI-7 is ongoing adversarial testing.

questions.stem: An AI agent can read the CRM, send emails to customers and issue refunds. Following the MCSB AI controls, how should refunds above a set threshold be handled?
options: Require human approval before the agent completes the refund
Allow the agent to complete the refund and log it to Microsoft Sentinel
Give the agent Owner on the subscription so it can fix failures itself
Rely on the safety meta-prompt to tell the agent not to issue large refunds
questions.explain: AI-5 (human-in-the-loop) requires human review of critical actions such as financial transactions. Logging alone doesn't prevent harm, Owner breaks AI-4 least privilege, and meta-prompts (AI-3) can be bypassed by prompt injection, so they aren't sufficient alone.

questions.stem: Which TWO measures implement MCSB AI-2 (multi-layered content filtering) for a generative AI chat application? Select TWO.
options: Apply Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields to user input
Filter model output for harmful or sensitive content before returning it
Assign the app a system-assigned managed identity
Run a quarterly PyRIT red team exercise
Deploy the model in a private virtual network
questions.explain: AI-2 filters at input, processing and output stages, so input Prompt Shields and output filtering fit. Managed identity supports least privilege (AI-4), PyRIT is red teaming (AI-7), and private networking is platform security, not content filtering.

questions.case: Relecloud runs a customer support copilot on Azure OpenAI. The SOC wants real-time alerts when users attempt jailbreaks or when the app leaks sensitive data, with prompt evidence included and incidents correlated alongside endpoint and email alerts.
questions.stem: Which solution meets the requirement?
options: Defender CSPM AI security posture management
Azure Monitor metrics on the Azure OpenAI resource
Microsoft Defender for Cloud threat protection for AI services integrated with Defender XDR
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager AI assessments
questions.explain: Threat protection for AI services raises real-time alerts (jailbreak, data leakage) with prompt evidence and integrates with Defender XDR for correlation (MCSB AI-6). AI-SPM finds misconfigurations, not runtime attacks; metrics don't detect jailbreaks; Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls.

questions.stem: Which THREE are the guiding principles of Zero Trust? Select THREE.
options: Verify explicitly
Use least privilege access
Trust the corporate network
Assume breach
Defence at the perimeter only
questions.explain: Zero Trust rests on verify explicitly, use least privilege access, and assume breach. Trusting the corporate network and relying on perimeter-only defence are exactly the assumptions Zero Trust rejects.

questions.stem: Put the first stages of the Zero Trust adoption lifecycle in order.
options: Define strategy
Plan
Ready
Adopt
Govern
questions.explain: The lifecycle starts with Define strategy (business case), then Plan, Ready (prepare environment), Adopt (implement incrementally), then Govern (track and measure) and Manage.

questions.stem: Leadership wants to minimise the impact of a successful attack by limiting blast radius through segmentation, threat detection and response. Which Zero Trust adoption business scenario matches this goal?
options: Secure remote and hybrid work
Identify and protect sensitive business data
Meet regulatory and compliance requirements
Prevent or reduce business damage from a breach
questions.explain: 'Prevent or reduce business damage from a breach' focuses on limiting blast radius via segmentation, detection and response. Remote work focuses on users and devices, data protection on classification, and compliance on regulatory alignment.

questions.case: A healthcare company is starting its Zero Trust journey. Basic hygiene is weak: no MFA for many users, many standing admin accounts and an untested backup process. The CISO wants quick, visible risk reduction in the first 90 days before tackling bigger programmes.
questions.stem: Which approach best follows Microsoft's Zero Trust guidance?
options: Start with 'Rapidly modernize your security posture' and RaMP quick wins (access trust, ransomware recovery)
Start with a full network micro-segmentation project across all datacentres
Wait until all legacy systems are retired before adopting any Zero Trust controls
Start with the 'Meet regulatory and compliance requirements' scenario and buy a new GRC platform
questions.explain: 'Rapidly modernize your security posture' is typically the starting scenario, building basic hygiene, and RaMP checklists deliver fast wins like MFA/Conditional Access and recovery readiness. Large segmentation projects and waiting for legacy retirement delay risk reduction; a GRC platform doesn't fix hygiene.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Zero Trust adoption framework, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Each business scenario progresses through the adoption lifecycle independently.
The Define strategy stage focuses on building a business case tied to business risks and goals.
SecOps is not one of the Zero Trust technology pillars.

questions.explain: Scenarios move through the lifecycle on their own timelines, and Define strategy builds the business case. SecOps is a technology pillar alongside identities, endpoints, data, apps, infrastructure and network.

questions.stem: Which Zero Trust principle is MOST directly applied when Conditional Access evaluates user risk, device compliance and location before granting access to an app?
options: Assume breach
Use least privilege access
Verify explicitly
Segment access by network zone
questions.explain: Verify explicitly means authenticating and authorising on all available signals such as identity, device, location and risk. Least privilege limits what is granted, assume breach drives segmentation and detection, and network-zone trust is a legacy model.

questions.stem: The CAF AI security guidance recommends supplementing your existing threat modelling with which knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques specific to AI systems?
options: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
MITRE ATLAS
MITRE D3FEND
CIS Critical Security Controls
questions.explain: MITRE ATLAS catalogues adversary techniques against AI and ML systems, and CAF pairs it with OWASP generative AI guidance. ATT&CK for ICS covers industrial systems, D3FEND catalogues defensive techniques, and CIS Controls is a general control set.

questions.stem: You need an inventory (AI bill of materials) of generative AI workloads across Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, with attack paths showing exposed AI endpoints. Which plan must be enabled?
options: Defender for Cloud Foundational CSPM
Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender CSPM
Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explain: AI security posture management, including the AI BOM and AI attack paths across Azure, AWS and GCP, is delivered through Defender CSPM. Foundational CSPM lacks attack paths, Defender for Servers protects VMs, and Defender for Cloud Apps discovers SaaS apps.

questions.case: Proseware's employees are pasting customer data into public generative AI websites. Leadership wants to adopt AI safely: approved AI tools for staff, visibility of which AI apps are in use, and prevention of sensitive data leaving in prompts. Proseware has Microsoft 365 E5.
questions.stem: Which THREE actions should you include in the secure AI adoption strategy? Select THREE.
options: Use Defender for Cloud Apps to discover generative AI apps and block unsanctioned ones
Provide an approved AI assistant with user training, governed by an AI Center of Excellence
Apply Microsoft Purview DLP policies to prevent sensitive data being shared with AI apps
Block all AI apps permanently at the firewall without offering alternatives
Turn off audit logging to protect employee privacy
questions.explain: Discovery and control of AI apps, sanctioned tools with training and central governance, and DLP for prompts together reduce shadow AI. Blanket blocking without alternatives drives workarounds, and disabling audit removes the visibility needed to govern AI.

questions.stem: For each statement about securing AI workloads in Azure, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Using managed identities for AI app connections avoids storing credentials in code.
Defender for Cloud threat protection for AI services scans image and audio tokens as well as text.
Azure Private Link can restrict access to AI PaaS services to private endpoints.

questions.explain: Managed identities remove stored secrets, and Private Link keeps AI services off the public internet. Threat protection for AI services currently scans only text tokens, not image or audio.

questions.stem: Your organisation is deploying dozens of autonomous AI agents that call Microsoft Graph and line-of-business APIs. Security wants each agent to have its own governed identity that can be targeted by Conditional Access and lifecycle policies. What should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
A shared service account per department
One app registration with a client secret shared across all agents
Guest (B2B) accounts for each agent
questions.explain: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives AI agents their own identities that can be governed and protected like other identities. Shared accounts and shared secrets break least privilege and accountability, and B2B guest accounts are for external people.

questions.stem: Which CAF methodology produces Azure landing zones as its main output?
options: Strategy
Ready
Adopt
Manage
questions.explain: CAF Ready prepares the cloud environment, centred on Azure landing zones. Strategy defines business justification, Adopt migrates or innovates workloads, and Manage covers operations.

questions.stem: According to CAF, when should the Secure methodology be applied during cloud adoption?
options: Only after workloads are migrated, during the Manage phase
Only during Ready, when landing zones are built
Across every phase, from strategy through management
Only when an auditor requests evidence
questions.explain: CAF states security spans every methodology phase and gaps in any phase weaken posture, so Secure applies end to end. Limiting it to Ready, Manage or audits leaves gaps in strategy, planning and adoption.

questions.stem: Put the CAF Govern steps in order.
options: Build a cloud governance team
Assess cloud risks
Document cloud governance policies
Enforce cloud governance policies
Monitor cloud governance
questions.explain: CAF Govern first forms a team, assesses risks, documents policies addressing those risks, enforces them (preferably automated with Azure Policy), then monitors compliance and adjusts.

questions.case: A global insurer is evaluating its cloud governance. It has a 60-page policy document stating that storage accounts must not allow public access and that resources must be deployed only in two approved regions. Audits find that 30% of new resources break these rules, and no one is notified.
questions.stem: Which gap in the CAF Govern methodology is MOST evident, and what is the fix?
options: Missing strategy; write a new business case
Missing incident response; create a Sentinel playbook to delete non-compliant resources
Missing landing zones; move all workloads into the Sandbox management group
Missing enforcement; implement Azure Policy deny and audit assignments at management group scope
questions.explain: Policies exist on paper but aren't enforced or monitored. CAF recommends automated enforcement, such as Azure Policy deny for public access and allowed locations at management group scope. A business case or Sandbox move doesn't enforce, and deleting resources via playbook is reactive and risky.

questions.stem: For each statement about CAF and WAF, select Yes if true.

statements.s: CAF focuses on the organisation and cloud estate, while WAF focuses on individual workloads.
CAF Secure recommends aligning security modernisation with the Zero Trust adoption framework.
The CIA triad stands for control, inspection and authentication.

questions.explain: CAF is estate-level and WAF is workload-level, and CAF Secure points to the Zero Trust adoption framework. The CIA triad is confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.stem: Which TWO are pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework? Select TWO.
options: Operational Excellence
Governance
Cost Optimization
Compliance
Identity
questions.explain: The five WAF pillars are Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence and Performance Efficiency. Governance is a CAF methodology, and compliance and identity are topics within pillars, not pillars themselves.

questions.stem: A WAF assessment of an App Service workload finds database connection strings stored in plain text in application settings. Which WAF Security checklist recommendation does this finding fall under?
options: SE:03 Classify and apply data labels
SE:06 Isolate, filter and control network traffic
SE:09 Protect application secrets
SE:12 Define and test incident response procedures
questions.explain: SE:09 covers protecting application secrets, for example storing them in Key Vault accessed by managed identity. SE:03 is data classification, SE:06 is network control, and SE:12 is incident response.

questions.case: A trading platform team must add TLS inspection through Azure Firewall Premium for all outbound traffic. The Performance Efficiency lead warns about added latency and the finance lead about cost. The security lead says inspection is required by the company's baseline.
questions.stem: How should the architect handle this according to the Well-Architected Framework?
options: Always choose the Security option because Security overrides all other pillars
Drop inspection because Performance Efficiency is the priority for trading
Postpone the decision until after go-live
Evaluate and document the trade-off, scoping inspection to required traffic and measuring its impact
questions.explain: WAF expects explicit, documented trade-offs between pillars, balancing risk against cost and performance, for example scoping inspection. No pillar automatically wins, and deferring past go-live leaves the baseline unmet.

questions.stem: A workload team wants a structured self-assessment that scores their architecture against each Well-Architected pillar and produces prioritised recommendations. What should they use?
options: Azure Well-Architected Review
Microsoft Secure Score
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Azure Migrate assessment
questions.explain: The Azure Well-Architected Review assesses a workload against the pillars. Secure Score measures security posture only, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and Azure Migrate assesses servers for migration readiness and sizing.

questions.stem: Which Azure Policy effect prevents a non-compliant resource from being created or updated?
options: Deny
Audit
Modify
AuditIfNotExists
questions.explain: Deny blocks the create or update request. Audit and AuditIfNotExists only record non-compliance, and Modify changes properties (such as tags) rather than blocking the request.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure Policy rule so that diagnostic settings are deployed automatically to Key Vaults that don't have them.
options: auditIfNotExists
deny
deployIfNotExists
append
questions.explain: deployIfNotExists deploys a related resource when it is missing, using roleDefinitionIds and a deployment template. auditIfNotExists only reports, deny blocks requests, and append adds fields to the request rather than deploying a related resource.

questions.stem: Your company needs attack path analysis and the cloud security explorer for Azure and AWS resources. Which TWO statements are correct? Select TWO.
options: These capabilities require the Defender CSPM plan
Foundational CSPM includes attack path analysis at no cost
Attack path analysis can include connected AWS accounts when Defender CSPM is enabled on the connector
Cloud security explorer requires Microsoft Sentinel
Attack path analysis works only for Azure resources
questions.explain: Attack path analysis and cloud security explorer are Defender CSPM features and extend to AWS and GCP connectors with Defender CSPM enabled. Foundational CSPM gives recommendations and Secure Score only, and Sentinel isn't required.

questions.case: Fourth Coffee has 120 subscriptions. Each new application team gets Owner on its subscription. Security requires that every subscription has Defender for Cloud plans on, no public IPs on NICs in Corp workloads, and that application teams cannot weaken these settings.
questions.stem: Which design BEST meets the requirements?
options: Assign Policy initiatives at management groups; give app teams Contributor plus scoped roles, not Owner
Ask each team to configure the settings and run a monthly manual review
Give the security team Owner on every subscription and leave app teams as Owner
Use resource locks on every resource group
questions.explain: Policy at management group scope is inherited by all subscriptions and enforces settings; removing Owner prevents teams from changing policy assignments or RBAC. Manual reviews don't enforce, dual Owners leave teams able to undo settings, and locks block deletion, not configuration drift.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure CLI command that assigns a built-in policy initiative at management group scope.
questions.code:
az policy assignment create \
  --name mcsb-baseline \
  --policy-set-definition "1f3afdf9-d0c9-4c3d-847f-89da613e70a8" \
  ____ "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/contoso"
options: --resource-group
--scope
--management-group-id
--location
questions.explain: --scope takes the full resource ID of the assignment scope, here a management group. --resource-group targets a resource group, --location sets the managed identity location, and --management-group-id isn't a parameter of az policy assignment create.

questions.stem: In the Azure landing zone reference architecture, which management group holds subscriptions for shared services such as hub networking, central logging and domain controllers?
options: Landing zones
Sandbox
Platform
Decommissioned
questions.explain: Platform (with children such as Identity, Management and Connectivity) hosts shared services run by the platform team. Landing zones hosts workloads, Sandbox is for experimentation, and Decommissioned holds cancelled subscriptions.

questions.stem: A team proposes creating Dev, Test and Prod management groups under Landing zones so each environment gets different policies. What does the Azure landing zone guidance recommend?
options: Create the three management groups as proposed
Create separate tenants for Dev, Test and Prod
Put all environments in one subscription with tags
Separate environments into different subscriptions within the same management group
questions.explain: CAF advises not to create management groups for environments; use separate subscriptions in the same management group (for example Corp). Separate tenants add heavy overhead, and one subscription with tags gives weak isolation.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure landing zones, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Internet-facing workloads typically go under the Online management group.
A management group hierarchy supports up to ten levels below the root.
Setting a default management group stops new subscriptions landing directly under the tenant root.

questions.explain: Online is for internet-facing workloads and Corp for private, hub-connected ones. The hierarchy supports six levels of depth (not counting root and subscription), and a default management group places new subscriptions in a governed location.

questions.case: A retailer's application teams request 10-20 new subscriptions a month. Each must be placed in the right management group, peered to the hub, given budgets and RBAC, and covered by Defender for Cloud and logging policies on day one. Manual setup takes three weeks and is inconsistent.
questions.stem: What should the architect recommend?
options: Subscription vending using infrastructure as code to create pre-governed application landing zones
Give application teams Owner at the intermediate root so they can create their own subscriptions
Place all new workloads in the Sandbox management group until the platform team has time
Use a single shared subscription for all application teams
questions.explain: Subscription vending automates creation of standardised, policy-governed application landing zones. Owner at the intermediate root breaks least privilege, Sandbox is not for production, and a shared subscription removes isolation and blurs ownership.

questions.stem: Put the levels of the Azure landing zone management group hierarchy in order, from the top.
options: Tenant Root Group
Intermediate root management group
Landing zones management group
Corp management group
Workload subscription
questions.explain: The tenant root group contains the intermediate root, which contains Landing zones; Corp is a child of Landing zones, and workload subscriptions sit inside Corp.

questions.stem: Which testing technique analyses source code for vulnerabilities without running the application?
options: Dynamic application security testing (DAST)
Penetration testing
Static application security testing (SAST)
Chaos engineering
questions.explain: SAST, such as CodeQL, analyses code at build time without execution. DAST and penetration testing probe a running application, and chaos engineering tests resilience by injecting faults.

questions.stem: Complete the GitHub Actions workflow so the job can sign in to Azure with workload identity federation (OIDC) instead of a stored client secret.
options: id-token
secrets
actions
deployments
questions.explain: OIDC login needs the id-token: write permission so the job can request a federated token from GitHub. 'actions' and 'deployments' are unrelated permission scopes, and 'secrets' is not a valid workflow permission.

questions.stem: Your organisation connects Azure DevOps to Defender for Cloud. Which TWO capabilities require Defender CSPM rather than Foundational CSPM? Select TWO.
options: Pull request annotations
Exposed secrets findings
Code-to-cloud mapping for containers
IaC misconfiguration findings
Inventory of DevOps resources
questions.explain: PR annotations and code-to-cloud mapping are Defender CSPM features. Secrets, IaC misconfiguration findings and DevOps inventory are available with Foundational CSPM.

questions.case: A software company is adopting DevSecOps aligned with CAF. Developers complain that security reviews happen only before release and delay launches by weeks. Recent issues included a hard-coded storage key pushed to GitHub and a vulnerable open-source library found in production.
questions.stem: Which change BEST addresses both issues while reducing release delays?
options: Add a manual security sign-off meeting before each production release
Move all source code to a private Azure Repos project
Run a DAST scan in production once a year
Shift left: secret scanning with push protection, PR dependency scanning, design-time threat modelling
questions.explain: Shifting left catches secrets before they're pushed and vulnerable dependencies in PRs, and threat modelling moves design review earlier, reducing late delays. More sign-offs add delay, yearly DAST is too infrequent and misses secrets, and private repos don't stop committed secrets or vulnerable packages.

questions.stem: Your organization uses Microsoft Defender XDR for endpoints, email and identities. You must also detect attacks using Palo Alto firewall logs and AWS CloudTrail, and analysts want one incident queue. What should you recommend?
options: Deploy Microsoft Sentinel, connect Defender XDR, and onboard Sentinel to the Microsoft Defender portal
Enable Defender for Cloud Apps and connect the firewall as an app connector
Create Defender XDR custom detection rules over the firewall logs
Deploy a second Defender XDR tenant dedicated to third-party logs
questions.explain: Sentinel (SIEM) ingests third-party and multicloud logs; onboarding it to the Defender portal with the Defender XDR connector gives a single incident queue. Defender XDR alone doesn't ingest arbitrary firewall logs, Defender for Cloud Apps uses firewall logs only for Shadow IT discovery, and a second tenant splits rather than unifies operations.

questions.stem: For each statement about XDR and SIEM in Microsoft security operations, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft Defender XDR correlates alerts from Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Identity into incidents.
Microsoft Sentinel requires all data to come from Microsoft products.
Microsoft Sentinel can be used in the Microsoft Defender portal together with Defender XDR.

questions.explain: Defender XDR natively correlates its products' alerts into incidents. Sentinel is a SIEM that ingests data from any source, including third-party appliances and other clouds. Sentinel can be onboarded to the Defender portal for unified security operations with Defender XDR.

questions.case: Fabrikam runs Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR. The CFO wants Sentinel ingestion costs cut without losing incident visibility. Today Fabrikam streams every Defender XDR advanced hunting table (DeviceEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents, EmailEvents and others) into the analytics tier for 2 years, although analysts only query them during investigations from the last 30 days.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions should you recommend to reduce cost while keeping incident visibility? Select TWO.
options: Keep the Defender XDR incidents and alerts connector enabled
Stop streaming raw XDR tables you don't need for custom detections and query them in advanced hunting instead
Disconnect the Defender XDR connector entirely
Move all data to Basic Audit in Microsoft Purview
Raise the analytics tier retention to 12 years
questions.explain: Defender XDR incidents and alerts are free to ingest and give visibility, so keep them. Raw advanced hunting tables are billed and are already queryable in the Defender portal for 30 days, so stream only what custom Sentinel detections need (long-term copies can go to the data lake tier). Disconnecting loses incidents; Purview Audit isn't a SIEM store; more retention costs more.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule type is designed to run approximately every minute for fast detection?
options: Scheduled query rule
Near-real-time (NRT) rule
Anomaly rule
Fusion rule
questions.explain: NRT rules run roughly once a minute for low-latency detection. Scheduled rules run at a configurable interval (minimum 5 minutes). Anomaly rules use machine learning baselines, and Fusion is the multistage attack correlation engine; neither is defined by a one-minute cadence.

questions.stem: A company with Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) asks how long user activity records are kept by default in the unified audit log. What do you answer?
options: 30 days
90 days
180 days
1 year
questions.explain: Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default (it was 90 days for records created before October 2023). One year is the Audit (Premium) default for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records. 30 days is the Defender XDR advanced hunting window, not Purview Audit.

questions.case: Contoso Bank must keep Exchange Online and SharePoint audit records for executives for seven years to satisfy a regulator, and investigators must be able to search them in Microsoft Purview. Executives already have Microsoft 365 E5 licences. Records from before the project start don't need to be retained.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Create an Audit (Standard) retention policy set to seven years
Assign executives the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on and a 10-year audit retention policy
Enable Audit (Premium) only, because it extends retention to 10 years automatically
Export the audit log monthly to a CSV file in a SharePoint site with a retention label
questions.explain: Retention beyond one year needs Audit (Premium) (included in E5) plus the per-user 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on and a matching policy; it isn't retroactive, which matches the requirement. Standard has no custom retention policies, Premium alone defaults to one year, and CSV exports aren't searchable in Purview Audit.

questions.stem: An investigator needs to search the Microsoft 365 unified audit log from Exchange Online PowerShell for MailItemsAccessed events for one user over the last 30 days. Complete the command.
questions.code: ____ -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) -EndDate (Get-Date) -Operations MailItemsAccessed -UserIds ceo@contoso.com -ResultSize 5000
options: Search-AdminAuditLog
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig
Get-MessageTrace
questions.explain: Search-UnifiedAuditLog queries the Purview unified audit log and supports -Operations and -UserIds. Search-AdminAuditLog covers only Exchange admin cmdlet activity, Get-AdminAuditLogConfig shows audit settings, and Get-MessageTrace tracks mail flow rather than audited activities.

questions.stem: A global company plans one Microsoft Sentinel workspace per business unit (12 in total) so each unit sees only its own data. All data can legally stay in one region. What should you recommend instead?
options: Keep 12 workspaces and use Azure Lighthouse to join them
Use a single workspace with resource-context and table-level RBAC to separate access
Use a single workspace and give every analyst the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role on it
Create 12 Microsoft 365 tenants, one per business unit
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends the fewest workspaces possible; access separation is achieved with resource-context RBAC and table-level RBAC. Lighthouse is for cross-tenant management, not access separation inside one tenant. Workspace-wide Reader shows everything to everyone, and new tenants add huge overhead.

questions.stem: You must protect 300 on-premises Windows servers with Microsoft Defender for Servers and apply Azure Policy machine configuration to them. What must you deploy first?
options: Azure Arc agent (Connected Machine agent) on each server
The Log Analytics agent (MMA) on each server
A site-to-site VPN to an Azure virtual network
Azure Bastion in the on-premises network
questions.explain: Azure Arc projects non-Azure servers into Azure Resource Manager, which lets Defender for Servers, Azure Policy and extensions manage them. The Log Analytics agent is retired. A VPN gives connectivity but no resource projection, and Azure Bastion is an Azure PaaS jump service, not an on-premises onboarding tool.

questions.stem: You are configuring the Microsoft Sentinel Amazon Web Services S3 connector to ingest CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs. Which TWO AWS components are part of the design? Select TWO.
options: An SQS queue that receives notifications of new log files
An IAM role that Sentinel assumes through an OIDC web identity provider
An AWS Direct Connect circuit to Azure
An Azure Arc agent installed on CloudTrail
A Kinesis data stream pushing events to Event Hubs
questions.explain: The S3 connector reads logs from S3 buckets after being notified through SQS, using an IAM role trusted via an OIDC web identity provider. No private circuit is needed; Arc is for servers and Kubernetes, not AWS managed services; Kinesis-to-Event Hubs isn't how this connector works.

questions.stem: You need a Sentinel query listing non-Azure machines (on-premises or other clouds) that have reported to the workspace in the last day, to verify agent coverage. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ComputerEnvironment == "Non-Azure"
| summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, OSType
options: SecurityEvent
Heartbeat
AzureActivity
SigninLogs
questions.explain: The Heartbeat table records agent check-ins and includes ComputerEnvironment and OSType, making it the right table for coverage checks. SecurityEvent holds Windows security events only, AzureActivity holds control-plane operations, and SigninLogs holds Entra ID sign-ins.

questions.stem: Analysts want every incident created by the 'Brute force against Azure Portal' rule to be tagged, assigned to the Tier 1 group and given a standard checklist. No external systems are involved. What should you use?
options: A Logic Apps playbook triggered by the alert
A Defender XDR custom detection rule
A Sentinel watchlist
A Sentinel automation rule
questions.explain: Automation rules can tag, assign owners and add task lists to incidents without code. A playbook is meant for cross-system orchestration and is overkill here. Custom detection rules create alerts rather than manage incidents, and watchlists are reference data for queries.

questions.stem: You need high-severity Sentinel incidents to automatically open a ServiceNow ticket. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a Logic Apps playbook with the Microsoft Sentinel incident trigger and a ServiceNow action
Grant the Sentinel service account Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group
Create an automation rule for incidents with severity High that runs the playbook
Test with a sample high-severity incident and check the playbook run history
questions.explain: Build the playbook first, then grant Sentinel permission to run playbooks in that resource group (otherwise the automation rule can't trigger it), then create the automation rule that calls it, and finally test end to end.

questions.stem: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are built on which Azure service?
options: Azure Functions
Azure Automation runbooks
Azure Logic Apps
Azure Data Factory
questions.explain: Sentinel playbooks are Azure Logic Apps workflows (Consumption or Standard) using the Sentinel trigger and connectors. Functions and Automation runbooks can be called from a playbook but aren't the playbook platform; Data Factory is for data pipelines.

questions.case: Tailspin wants ransomware attacks contained within minutes even when no analyst is online at night. It uses Defender XDR (all workloads) and Sentinel in the Defender portal. Its devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint and users are in Entra ID.
questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it meets the requirement appropriately.

statements.s: Automatic attack disruption in Defender XDR can contain compromised assets during a high-confidence ransomware attack without analyst action.
Automated investigation and response (AIR) can be configured to remediate threats automatically on devices.
A Sentinel automation rule alone can isolate a Defender for Endpoint device without any playbook or built-in action.

questions.explain: Attack disruption automatically contains devices and users during high-confidence attacks, and AIR's automation level can be set to full remediation. Automation rules manage incidents (assign, tag, close, run playbooks); device isolation needs a playbook calling the Defender for Endpoint API or Defender's own response actions.

questions.stem: Put the phases of the incident response lifecycle (NIST SP 800-61) in order.
options: Preparation
Detection and analysis
Containment, eradication and recovery
Post-incident activity (lessons learned)
questions.explain: NIST's lifecycle starts with preparation, then detection and analysis, then containment, eradication and recovery, and ends with post-incident activity whose lessons feed back into preparation.

questions.case: During a human-operated ransomware incident at Litware, investigators find the attacker has Global Administrator rights and has been reading the security team's mailboxes. The CISO asks for the first design decision for running the response.
questions.stem: What should you recommend first?
options: Email all staff from the corporate tenant explaining the incident
Restore all servers from the most recent backup immediately
Wipe all endpoints using Intune before investigating
Move incident communications to an out-of-band channel separate from the compromised tenant
questions.explain: When the attacker controls identity and can read mail, responders must communicate out of band so their plans aren't seen. Corporate email is compromised; restoring before scoping and evicting the attacker risks reinfection from tainted backups or persistence; wiping destroys evidence and doesn't remove the attacker's cloud admin access.

questions.stem: A hunter's hypothesis is that attackers delete volume shadow copies before encryption. Complete the Defender XDR advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
____
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete shadows"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
options: DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceFileEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
IdentityLogonEvents
questions.explain: DeviceProcessEvents records process creation with FileName and ProcessCommandLine, which is what this hypothesis needs. DeviceNetworkEvents covers connections, DeviceFileEvents covers file creation/modification, and IdentityLogonEvents covers authentication events from Defender for Identity and Entra.

questions.stem: A hunting query finds a reliable pattern of credential theft that no current rule detects. Which TWO actions turn the hunt into ongoing protection? Select TWO.
options: Create a Defender XDR custom detection rule from the query
Create a Microsoft Sentinel scheduled analytics rule from the query and map it to the ATT&CK technique
Save the results as a bookmark only
Add the query results to a watchlist
Run the query in Livestream once
questions.explain: Operationalising a hunt means converting it into a scheduled detection: a custom detection rule in Defender XDR or an analytics rule in Sentinel, tagged with MITRE techniques. Bookmarks capture evidence, watchlists store reference data, and a single Livestream session watches temporarily; none provides ongoing detection.

questions.stem: A water utility wants to measure detection coverage for attacks that manipulate PLC set points and inhibit safety responses in its plants. Which framework view should it map its Defender for IoT detections to?
options: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise
MITRE ATT&CK Mobile
MITRE D3FEND
questions.explain: ATT&CK for ICS covers industrial control systems, with tactics such as Impair Process Control and Inhibit Response Function. Enterprise covers IT systems and cloud, Mobile covers Android and iOS, and D3FEND is a catalogue of defensive countermeasures rather than adversary behaviour.

questions.stem: For each statement about evaluating coverage with the MITRE ATT&CK page in Microsoft Sentinel, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Active coverage is based on the scheduled and NRT analytics rules enabled in the workspace.
Simulated coverage shows what coverage you could have by enabling available rules that aren't configured yet.
The goal of a coverage review is to place an enabled rule in every technique cell regardless of threat relevance.

questions.explain: The MITRE page shows active coverage from enabled scheduled and NRT rules, and simulated coverage from available but unconfigured rules. Coverage work should be prioritised by threats relevant to the organization; chasing every cell creates noise without reducing real risk.

questions.stem: You will deploy 200 instances of an autonomous procurement agent, all created from the same Microsoft Entra Agent ID blueprint. Any instance flagged high risk must be blocked, including instances created next year. What should the Conditional Access policy target?
options: All users
The agent identity blueprint
A security group containing the current agent identities
The Office 365 cloud app
questions.explain: A policy targeting the blueprint applies to every agent identity created from it, including future ones. 'All users' doesn't cover agents, a static group misses new instances (and group membership isn't how agent users are scoped), and targeting a resource doesn't express 'these agents'.

questions.case: Northwind builds an AI assistant that reads a user's mailbox on the user's behalf (delegated) and also runs nightly app-only jobs against SharePoint. Some downstream systems require the agent to have its own user account.
questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: For the delegated mailbox calls, Conditional Access policies targeting the signed-in user apply.
A Conditional Access policy assigned to 'All users' also covers the agent's user account.
The agent identity stores its own client secret, separate from the blueprint.

questions.explain: In on-behalf-of flows the token subject is the user, so user policies apply. Agent user accounts aren't covered by policies scoped through the Users assignment; you target them under Agents. Agent identities have no credentials of their own; the blueprint holds them.

questions.stem: A developer team wants its agent to call a third-party API using a static API key rather than Microsoft Entra tokens. Security requires Conditional Access to govern every agent call. What is the design issue?
options: API keys must be stored in Managed HSM rather than Key Vault
The agent must be assigned an Entra ID P2 licence
Calls using an API key bypass the Entra token pipeline, so Conditional Access can't evaluate them
API keys are only supported for agent user accounts
questions.explain: Conditional Access is evaluated when Entra ID issues tokens; an agent that authenticates with an API key never requests an Entra token, so policy can't apply. Storage location or licence doesn't change that, and API keys aren't an agent user feature.

questions.stem: A company wants to retire its VPN. Remote staff must reach an on-premises ERP (custom TCP protocol) and file shares, with Conditional Access requiring a compliant device. What should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
Azure VPN Gateway point-to-site with certificate authentication
Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Microsoft Entra Private Access
questions.explain: Entra Private Access provides Zero Trust per-app access to private TCP/UDP apps and file shares with Conditional Access. Application Proxy publishes only web (HTTP/HTTPS) apps. A point-to-site VPN is what they're retiring and grants network-level access, and Internet Access secures traffic to internet and SaaS destinations.

questions.stem: Engineers use AWS and Google Cloud consoles with separate local accounts. You need one identity, MFA enforced by Conditional Access, and automatic deprovisioning when people leave. Which TWO capabilities should you use? Select TWO.
options: SAML single sign-on from Microsoft Entra ID to AWS IAM Identity Center and Google Cloud
SCIM provisioning from Microsoft Entra ID to those platforms
Azure Lighthouse delegation to the AWS account
Defender for Cloud agentless scanning
B2B direct connect with AWS
questions.explain: Federated SAML SSO brings sign-ins through Entra ID so Conditional Access and MFA apply, and SCIM provisioning creates and removes accounts automatically. Lighthouse manages Azure resources across tenants only, agentless scanning is a posture feature, and B2B direct connect works only between Entra tenants.

questions.stem: An Azure Function must read secrets from Azure Key Vault without any credential stored in code or configuration. What should it use?
options: A managed identity with the Key Vault Secrets User role
A client secret stored in app settings
A shared access signature (SAS) token
A storage account access key
questions.explain: A managed identity has no secret to store and can be granted the Key Vault Secrets User RBAC role. A client secret in app settings is a stored credential, and SAS tokens and storage account keys are for Azure Storage, not Key Vault.

questions.case: Adatum acquired a company whose Active Directory forest has no network connectivity or trust with Adatum's forest. Adatum wants the acquired users in its Microsoft Entra tenant within weeks, with no new sync servers to maintain and high availability for the sync service.
questions.stem: Which synchronization design should you recommend for the acquired forest?
options: Add the forest to the existing Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server
Use B2B collaboration invitations for all acquired users
Create a forest trust and then use Entra Connect Sync
Install Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync agents in the acquired forest
questions.explain: Cloud Sync handles disconnected forests natively with lightweight agents managed from the cloud, and multiple agents give high availability. Connect Sync needs line of sight to every forest it syncs, a trust adds time and risk, and B2B makes them guests rather than members of the tenant.

questions.stem: A company federates with AD FS and wants to reduce attack surface and keep cloud sign-in working if the datacenter is offline. Which TWO actions should you recommend? Select TWO.
options: Enable password hash synchronization
Migrate domains from federation to cloud authentication using staged rollout
Deploy additional AD FS servers in a second datacenter
Switch to pass-through authentication as the only method
Disable Seamless SSO
questions.explain: Password hash sync authenticates in the cloud, survives on-premises outages and enables leaked credential detection; staged rollout moves users off AD FS safely. More AD FS servers keep the golden-SAML attack surface, PTA still depends on on-premises agents, and disabling Seamless SSO doesn't address either goal.

questions.stem: For each statement about hybrid identity, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Password hash synchronization enables Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials for synced users.
With pass-through authentication, an outage of all on-premises agents prevents cloud sign-in for those users.
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync supports device writeback.

questions.explain: PHS gives Entra ID hashes to compare with leaked credential sets. PTA validates passwords on premises, so losing all agents breaks sign-in. Device writeback isn't supported by Cloud Sync (Microsoft points to Cloud Kerberos trust instead).

questions.stem: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys infrastructure to Azure. Security forbids storing any Azure credential in GitHub. What should you configure?
options: A service principal certificate uploaded as a GitHub secret
A system-assigned managed identity on the GitHub runner
A federated identity credential on an app registration, trusting the repository and branch
A personal access token for an Azure DevOps service connection
questions.explain: Workload identity federation lets GitHub's OIDC token be exchanged for an Entra token, so no secret is stored. A certificate in GitHub is still a stored credential, GitHub-hosted runners aren't Azure resources so can't have a system-assigned managed identity, and a PAT is a stored secret for a different service.

questions.stem: For each statement about Conditional Access for workload identities, select Yes if true.

statements.s: It requires Workload Identities Premium licensing to create or modify the policies.
It can enforce a policy on managed identities.
Block access is the grant control available for these policies.

questions.explain: Workload identity CA needs Workload Identities Premium, applies to single-tenant service principals registered in your tenant (not managed identities or multitenant SaaS apps), and its only grant control is Block access, triggered by location or service principal risk.

questions.case: Proseware runs 50 Linux servers in an on-premises datacenter and 30 in AWS. Scripts on these servers call Azure Storage and Key Vault using client secrets stored in config files. A recent incident leaked one secret. Proseware wants to eliminate secrets for these calls and manage the servers from Azure.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Onboard the servers to Azure Arc and use the Arc-enabled server's managed identity
Move the client secrets into environment variables
Replace client secrets with storage account keys rotated monthly
Create B2B guest accounts for each server
questions.explain: Azure Arc-enabled servers get a system-assigned managed identity that can be granted RBAC on Storage and Key Vault without secrets, and Arc also lets Azure manage them. Environment variables still hold secrets, account keys are even broader secrets, and guest accounts are for people from other organizations.

questions.stem: Partner users already complete MFA in their own Microsoft Entra tenant but are prompted again when accessing your apps as B2B guests. Your Conditional Access requires MFA for guests. What should you configure?
options: Inbound trust settings in cross-tenant access settings to trust MFA from the partner tenant
Exclude guest users from the MFA policy
Outbound access settings for the partner tenant
Tenant restrictions v2
questions.explain: Inbound trust settings let your tenant accept the partner's MFA claim, so your policy is satisfied without a second prompt. Excluding guests removes protection, outbound settings govern your users going to other tenants, and tenant restrictions v2 controls which external accounts your users can use on your devices.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra External ID, select Yes if true.

statements.s: B2B direct connect is blocked by default and must be enabled by both organizations.
B2B collaboration users are represented as guest user objects in the resource tenant.
By default, your tenant trusts MFA and compliant-device claims from all other Microsoft Entra organizations.

questions.explain: B2B direct connect requires mutual configuration and is off by default. B2B collaboration creates guest objects. Default inbound trust settings don't trust other organizations' MFA or device claims; you must enable trust explicitly.

questions.case: Woodgrove and its subsidiary run separate Microsoft Entra tenants. 3,000 subsidiary employees need to appear automatically as users in Woodgrove's tenant for Teams and apps, be removed when they leave, and not receive invitation emails or consent prompts.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Bulk B2B invitations with a PowerShell script each month
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync from the subsidiary's tenant
Cross-tenant synchronization with automatic redemption enabled in both tenants
B2B direct connect only
questions.explain: Cross-tenant synchronization automates creating and removing B2B users across tenants of a multitenant organization, and automatic redemption (both outbound and inbound) suppresses consent prompts. Scripted invites are manual and send emails, Entra Connect syncs from AD DS not from another tenant, and direct connect doesn't create user objects.

questions.stem: Help desk staff are being socially engineered into resetting MFA for impostors. You want callers to prove their identity with a credential issued after HR identity proofing, held in a wallet on their phone. What should you recommend?
options: Self-service password reset with security questions
SMS one-time passcode to the number on file
B2B collaboration with email one-time passcode
Microsoft Entra Verified ID verifiable credentials presented from Microsoft Authenticator
questions.explain: Verified ID lets the organization issue a verifiable credential that the employee holds in Authenticator and presents to the help desk verifier, which defeats impersonation. Security questions and SMS codes are weak and phishable, and B2B email OTP is a guest sign-in method rather than identity proofing.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a Microsoft Entra Verified ID exchange in order.
options: The issuer verifies the person and issues a signed verifiable credential
The holder stores the credential in Microsoft Authenticator
A verifier requests a presentation and the holder shares the credential
The verifier validates the signature against the issuer's decentralized identifier
questions.explain: The issuer signs and issues the credential, the holder keeps it in a wallet, the verifier requests it and the holder presents it, and finally the verifier checks the signature using the issuer's DID (did:web) without calling the issuer.

questions.stem: Which methods satisfy the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength? Select THREE.
options: FIDO2 security key
Windows Hello for Business
Microsoft Authenticator push notification
Certificate-based authentication (multifactor)
SMS one-time passcode
questions.explain: The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength includes FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business or platform credentials, and multifactor certificate-based authentication. Authenticator push and SMS satisfy the general MFA strength but can be relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing.

questions.stem: Users may open a SharePoint site labelled Highly Confidential only after phishing-resistant MFA from a compliant device. Other sites need only standard MFA. What should you use to target the stricter policy?
options: A Conditional Access authentication context linked to the sensitivity label
A named location for the SharePoint site
A device filter on the Office 365 app
A separate tenant for the confidential site
questions.explain: Authentication context lets a CA policy apply to a specific resource, such as a SharePoint site whose sensitivity label references context c1. Named locations describe network origins, a device filter describes devices rather than content, and a separate tenant is unnecessary overhead.

questions.stem: You are reviewing a Conditional Access policy created through Microsoft Graph that must block legacy authentication clients. Complete the conditions section.
options: ["browser", "mobileAppsAndDesktopClients"]
["exchangeActiveSync", "other"]
["all"]
["browser"]
questions.explain: Legacy authentication clients are represented by the clientAppTypes values exchangeActiveSync and other. Browser and mobileAppsAndDesktopClients are modern authentication clients, so blocking them (or 'all') would block every user.

questions.stem: For each statement about continuous access evaluation (CAE), select Yes if true.

statements.s: A CAE-capable resource such as Exchange Online can reject a token soon after the user's account is disabled, before the token would normally expire.
CAE enforces country/region-based named locations in real time.
CAE-capable sessions can receive long-lived tokens of up to 28 hours.

questions.explain: CAE resources react to critical events such as account disablement. Real-time location enforcement works only with IP-based named locations; country locations aren't evaluated instantly. Because revocation is event-driven, CAE tokens can last up to 28 hours.

questions.stem: You must ensure that any administrator who creates, updates or deletes a Conditional Access policy first completes phishing-resistant MFA, no matter how they got the permission. What should you implement?
options: A PIM activation setting requiring MFA
A Conditional Access policy targeting the Conditional Access Administrator directory role
Protected actions mapped to a Conditional Access authentication context
An access review of Conditional Access Administrators
questions.explain: Protected actions attach an authentication context (and its CA policy) to specific permissions, enforced when the action is attempted regardless of role or how it was obtained. PIM enforces only at activation, a role-targeted policy misses custom roles or other paths, and access reviews don't enforce authentication.

questions.case: Relecloud still uses the legacy user risk and sign-in risk policies in Microsoft Entra ID Protection. It holds Entra ID P2. The security lead wants risk-based protection to continue past the legacy policy retirement and to follow Microsoft's current recommendations.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Create one Conditional Access policy combining user risk High and sign-in risk Medium with Block access
Separate CA policies (user risk High: risk remediation; sign-in risk Medium+High: MFA), then disable legacy
Keep the legacy policies and enable security defaults
Configure CAE strict location enforcement instead of risk policies
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends separate risk-based CA policies (not combined conditions): require risk remediation for high user risk and MFA for medium/high sign-in risk, tested in report-only, then disable the legacy policies, which retire on 1 October 2026. Blocking stops self-remediation, security defaults conflict with CA, and CAE doesn't replace risk policies.

questions.stem: You need to find successful sign-ins in the last 7 days where no Conditional Access policy applied, to discover gaps in your Zero Trust coverage. Complete the KQL query.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where ____ == "notApplied"
| summarize Count = count() by AppDisplayName, UserPrincipalName
options: RiskState
AuthenticationRequirement
ConditionalAccessStatus
ClientAppUsed
questions.explain: ConditionalAccessStatus records success, failure or notApplied for each sign-in. RiskState is ID Protection risk, AuthenticationRequirement shows single- or multifactor, and ClientAppUsed identifies the client type; none indicates whether a policy applied.

questions.case: During a Zero Trust review at Fourth Coffee you find: a 'Require MFA' policy excludes a 400-member 'VIP' group; legacy authentication isn't blocked; admin roles accept any MFA method; two emergency access accounts are excluded from all policies and monitored.
questions.stem: Which THREE findings should you flag as gaps against Zero Trust? Select THREE.
options: The broad VIP group exclusion from MFA
Legacy authentication isn't blocked
Admin roles don't require phishing-resistant MFA
Emergency access accounts are excluded and monitored
Policies are named by persona
questions.explain: Broad exclusions, unblocked legacy auth (which can't do MFA) and weak MFA for admins all break 'verify explicitly'. Excluding monitored emergency access accounts is recommended to avoid lockout, and persona-based naming is Microsoft's recommended practice.

questions.stem: Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy, you want to see which existing policies would apply to a specific user signing in to a specific app from a given location, without the user signing in. What should you use?
options: Report-only mode
The Conditional Access What If tool
Sign-in logs
Access reviews
questions.explain: The What If tool simulates a sign-in with chosen user, app and conditions and lists the policies that would apply. Report-only and sign-in logs require real sign-ins to occur, and access reviews attest to access rather than evaluating policy.

questions.stem: You are writing AD DS hardening requirements. Which THREE should you include? Select THREE.
options: Deploy Windows LAPS to give every workstation and server a unique, rotated local administrator password
Use group managed service accounts (gMSA) for services
Install Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors on domain controllers and AD CS servers
Add all service accounts to the Protected Users group
Enable SMBv1 for compatibility on domain controllers
questions.explain: LAPS stops lateral movement with shared local admin passwords, gMSAs give long automatically rotated service passwords, and Defender for Identity detects identity attacks on DCs and AD CS. Protected Users breaks service accounts (no delegation or NTLM), and SMBv1 should be disabled.

questions.stem: You need Domain Admin accounts to be unable to use NTLM, unconstrained delegation or RC4 Kerberos encryption, with minimal configuration effort. What should you do?
options: Configure a fine-grained password policy for the admins
Enable Windows LAPS for the admin accounts
Add the accounts to the Protected Users security group
Mark the accounts as gMSAs
questions.explain: Protected Users membership automatically blocks NTLM, delegation and weak Kerberos encryption types for its members and shortens TGT lifetime. Fine-grained password policies set password rules, LAPS manages local (not domain) admin passwords, and gMSA is for service accounts, not people.

questions.case: Trey Research must store encryption keys for a payments platform. Regulators require that keys are held in a single-tenant HSM validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3, and that Azure subscription owners and management group admins can't grant themselves access to the keys.
questions.stem: Which service should you recommend?
options: Azure Key Vault Standard with access policies
Azure Key Vault Premium with HSM-backed keys
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
Azure Storage with Microsoft-managed keys
questions.explain: Managed HSM is single-tenant with its own security domain and local RBAC that higher Azure scopes can't override, on FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. Key Vault Premium is multitenant and governed by Azure RBAC, Standard uses software keys, and Microsoft-managed keys give the customer no custody.

questions.stem: A storage account will use a customer-managed key from an existing vault. The vault must not allow soft-deleted keys to be permanently removed before the retention period ends. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code: az keyvault update --name kv-payments-prod --resource-group rg-payments ____ true
options: --enable-soft-delete
--enable-rbac-authorization
--enable-purge-protection
--enabled-for-disk-encryption
questions.explain: Purge protection stops soft-deleted vaults and objects from being purged until retention expires, and CMK scenarios require it. Soft delete is already always on, RBAC authorization changes the access model, and enabled-for-disk-encryption lets Azure Disk Encryption retrieve secrets.

questions.stem: You are writing a design standard for Azure Key Vault across 40 applications. Which THREE practices should it include? Select THREE.
options: Use a separate vault per application, environment and region
Use Azure RBAC for data-plane access, such as Key Vault Secrets User for apps
Disable public network access and use private endpoints
Use one shared vault for all applications to simplify access policies
Grant developers Key Vault Administrator in production for troubleshooting
questions.explain: Separate vaults limit blast radius, Azure RBAC is the recommended model with least-privilege roles, and private endpoints remove public exposure. A single shared vault widens blast radius and access, and Key Vault Administrator for developers in production breaks least privilege.

questions.stem: In the enterprise access model, which plane should contain the Microsoft Entra Connect server, AD DS domain controllers and AD CS servers?
options: Data/workload plane
Management plane
User access
Control plane
questions.explain: Systems that control identity and access across the enterprise belong to the control plane (expanded Tier 0), because controlling them means controlling everything. The management plane is enterprise IT management, the workload plane holds apps and data, and user access is the former Tier 2 pathway.

questions.stem: Regional helpdesk staff in Germany must reset passwords only for German users. Today they hold User Administrator for the whole tenant. What should you recommend?
options: Assign Global Reader tenant-wide
Create a separate Entra tenant for Germany
Assign Password Administrator tenant-wide with PIM
Create an administrative unit for German users and assign Helpdesk Administrator scoped to it
questions.explain: Administrative units scope role assignments to a subset of objects, and Helpdesk Administrator is a smaller role than User Administrator. Global Reader can't reset passwords, a tenant-wide role (even through PIM) still covers every user, and a separate tenant is excessive.

questions.stem: For each statement about the enterprise access model, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The former Tier 1 is split into a management plane and a data/workload plane.
A data/workload plane administrator should be able to manage control plane systems to simplify operations.
Application (API) access is one of the access pathways the model protects.

questions.explain: Tier 1 splits into management and data/workload planes. Lower planes must never control higher ones, to prevent privilege escalation. The model covers user access, app (API) access and privileged access pathways.

questions.stem: Security Administrators must have no standing access, must activate for at most 4 hours, and must satisfy phishing-resistant MFA from a PAW at activation. Which PIM configuration meets this?
options: Permanent active assignment with MFA required on active assignment
Eligible assignments, 4-hour maximum activation, and a required CA authentication context on activation
Eligible assignments with ticket information required and no MFA
Active assignments expiring after 4 hours, renewed daily by a script
questions.explain: Eligible assignments remove standing access, maximum duration limits activation, and requiring an authentication context lets a CA policy enforce phishing-resistant MFA and a PAW device filter. Permanent active assignments keep standing access, ticket info alone isn't authentication, and scripted active assignments are standing privilege in disguise.

questions.stem: You are automating PIM so that a user becomes eligible (not active) for a Microsoft Entra role. Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell command.
questions.code:
$params = @{ action = "adminAssign"; justification = "Quarterly eligibility"; roleDefinitionId = $roleId; directoryScopeId = "/"; principalId = $userId; scheduleInfo = @{ startDateTime = (Get-Date); expiration = @{ type = "afterDuration"; duration = "P365D" } } }
____ -BodyParameter $params
options: New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignmentScheduleRequest
New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleEligibilityScheduleRequest
New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment
New-MgDirectoryRoleMemberByRef
questions.explain: Eligibility schedule requests create PIM eligible assignments. Assignment schedule requests create active assignments, New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment creates a direct (standing) assignment, and adding a directory role member by reference is the legacy permanent-membership method.

questions.case: Alpine Ski House needs just-in-time access for 30 engineers to a set of resources: Owner on two Azure subscriptions, membership of a group that grants admin access to a SaaS app, and the Exchange Administrator Entra role. All activations must require approval.
questions.stem: Which TWO PIM capabilities cover these requirements? Select TWO.
options: PIM for Azure resources
PIM for Groups
Entitlement management catalogs only
Azure Lighthouse eligible authorizations
Conditional Access session controls
questions.explain: PIM for Azure resources handles subscription Owner, and PIM for Groups handles just-in-time group membership for the SaaS app; Entra roles such as Exchange Administrator use PIM for Entra roles directly, or can be granted through a role-assignable group under PIM for Groups. Catalogs don't provide time-bound activation, Lighthouse is cross-tenant, and session controls don't grant roles.

questions.stem: What is the allowed range for the PIM 'Activation maximum duration' setting for a Microsoft Entra role?
options: 1 to 8 hours
15 minutes to 1 hour
1 to 24 hours
1 to 30 days
questions.explain: PIM lets you set activation maximum duration between 1 and 24 hours per role. Eligible and active assignment durations (which can be months or permanent) are separate settings from how long a single activation lasts.

questions.stem: Staff from a supplier, whose users sign in with their own Entra tenant, need to request access to a Teams team, a SharePoint site and an app together. Access must be approved by a sponsor and expire after 90 days. What should you recommend?
options: Invite each supplier user as a B2B guest and add them to groups manually
Enable B2B direct connect with the supplier
Use a dynamic group based on the supplier's domain
Create an access package in entitlement management with the supplier as a connected organization
questions.explain: An access package bundles the team, site and app, with a policy for a connected organization, sponsor approval and 90-day expiry; guest accounts are created on approval. Manual invites lack expiry and approval workflow, direct connect suits Teams shared channels only, and dynamic groups don't require approval.

questions.stem: Your tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P2 but not Microsoft Entra ID Governance. For each feature, select Yes if it is available.

statements.s: Basic entitlement management access packages with approval and expiration
Lifecycle workflows for joiner and leaver automation
Machine learning-assisted access review recommendations

questions.explain: Basic entitlement management is included in P2. Lifecycle workflows and machine learning-assisted access reviews are Entra ID Governance features; new IGA capabilities are added to Governance rather than P2.

questions.case: Bellows College wants new hires to receive a Temporary Access Pass on their first morning, be added to department groups automatically, and have licences and group memberships removed on their last day, without help desk tickets. HR data already flows into Entra ID.
questions.stem: Which capability should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Governance lifecycle workflows
Access reviews with auto-apply
PIM for Groups
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync scoping filters
questions.explain: Lifecycle workflows run joiner/leaver tasks such as generating a TAP, adding groups and removing access on schedule from HR attributes. Access reviews periodically attest existing access, PIM for Groups gives just-in-time membership, and sync scoping decides which objects synchronize.

questions.stem: A red team cracked service account passwords offline after requesting Kerberos service tickets for accounts with SPNs. Which mitigation directly addresses this attack?
options: Enable SMB signing on domain controllers
Reset the krbtgt account password twice
Replace the service accounts with group managed service accounts (gMSA)
Enable Windows LAPS on member servers
questions.explain: This is Kerberoasting; gMSAs have long, random, automatically rotated passwords that are infeasible to crack. SMB signing counters relay attacks, krbtgt resets counter Golden Tickets, and LAPS protects local administrator passwords rather than domain service accounts.

questions.stem: After confirming a Golden Ticket attack, you must invalidate forged tickets. Put the krbtgt recovery steps in order.
options: Contain the attacker's access to domain controllers and privileged accounts
Reset the krbtgt account password the first time
Wait for replication and the maximum ticket lifetime so legitimate tickets renew
Reset the krbtgt account password a second time
questions.explain: Contain first so the attacker can't steal the new key. A first reset still leaves the previous key valid, so wait for replication and ticket renewal to avoid outages, then reset again so tickets signed with the old key are rejected.

questions.stem: During an incident you need to retrieve the current Windows LAPS local administrator password that is backed up to AD DS for server SRV01. Complete the command.
questions.code: ____ -Identity SRV01 -AsPlainText
options: Get-LapsADPassword
Get-AdmPwdPassword
Get-LapsAADPassword
Reset-LapsPassword
questions.explain: Get-LapsADPassword retrieves Windows LAPS passwords stored in AD DS. Get-AdmPwdPassword belongs to legacy Microsoft LAPS, Get-LapsAADPassword reads passwords backed up to Microsoft Entra ID, and Reset-LapsPassword rotates the password on the local device instead of reading it.

questions.stem: Which TWO attacks against AD DS can Microsoft Defender for Identity detect? Select TWO.
options: Suspected DCSync (malicious replication request)
Suspected Golden Ticket usage
Malicious OAuth app consent in Microsoft 365
Phishing email with a malicious attachment
Container image vulnerability
questions.explain: Defender for Identity detects domain dominance attacks such as malicious replication (DCSync) and Golden Ticket activity. OAuth consent abuse is Defender for Cloud Apps app governance, phishing email is Defender for Office 365, and image vulnerabilities are Defender for Containers.

questions.stem: Your Global Administrators are on-premises AD DS accounts synced to Microsoft Entra ID. Why should you change this, and to what?
options: Synced admins can't use MFA; convert them to guest accounts
An AD DS compromise could take over the cloud; use cloud-only accounts for Entra privileged roles
Synced accounts can't be assigned roles; use service principals
Synced accounts exceed licence limits; use shared admin accounts
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends cloud-only accounts for privileged Entra roles so that an on-premises compromise can't pivot to the cloud through password or attribute changes. Synced accounts can use MFA and hold roles, guests are wrong for internal admins, and shared accounts destroy accountability.

questions.case: Lucerne Publishing outsources Microsoft 365 support to an MSP. Today the MSP has Global Administrator in Lucerne's tenant through a legacy delegated admin relationship. Lucerne wants least-privilege, time-bound partner access that it can review.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) with specific roles and an end date
Invite MSP staff as B2B guests with Global Administrator
Azure Lighthouse delegation for Microsoft 365
Share an emergency access account with the MSP
questions.explain: GDAP gives partners only the Entra roles they need for a limited duration, replacing broad legacy DAP. Guests with Global Administrator keep excessive privilege, Lighthouse covers Azure resource management rather than Microsoft 365 roles, and sharing break-glass credentials defeats their purpose.
