questions.stem: For each statement about emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID, select Yes if it reflects Microsoft guidance.

statements.s: Maintain at least two emergency access accounts.
Emergency access accounts should be synced from AD DS so they work if the cloud is unavailable.
Sign-ins by emergency access accounts should trigger alerts.

questions.explain: Microsoft recommends two or more cloud-only emergency access accounts with strong (for example FIDO2) authentication, excluded from most Conditional Access, and monitored so any use raises an alert. Syncing them from AD DS ties them to the on-premises environment they may need to bypass.

questions.stem: In 2026, a company running Azure, AWS and GCP wants Microsoft-native CIEM to find overprovisioned and inactive identities across all three clouds. What should you recommend?
options: Purchase Microsoft Entra Permissions Management
Enable the Defender CSPM plan in Microsoft Defender for Cloud and connect AWS and GCP
Use Azure Policy initiatives on AWS accounts
Use Microsoft Entra access reviews for AWS IAM roles
questions.explain: Entra Permissions Management was retired (support ended 1 October 2025); Microsoft points customers to Defender CSPM, which provides CIEM for Azure, AWS and GCP identities. Azure Policy doesn't evaluate AWS IAM natively, and access reviews cover Entra-integrated resources rather than AWS IAM permission usage.

questions.case: Defender CSPM shows that an AWS IAM role used by a build pipeline has AdministratorAccess but used only S3 and ECR actions in 90 days. The same role appears in an attack path from an internet-exposed EC2 instance.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions best reduce the risk? Select TWO.
options: Replace AdministratorAccess with a policy scoped to the S3 and ECR actions actually used
Remove the role from the exposed EC2 instance or close the instance's internet exposure
Add the role to an Entra access review
Increase CloudTrail log retention
Enable Defender for Storage on the S3 buckets only
questions.explain: Right-sizing to used permissions is the core CIEM remediation, and breaking the attack path (exposure or role attachment) removes the immediate route. Entra access reviews don't govern AWS IAM role permissions, longer retention aids investigation but not prevention, and Defender for Storage detects threats to data rather than shrinking the role.

questions.stem: Auditors require that users denied in a quarterly access review of a finance app lose access automatically, and that non-responding reviewers don't leave access in place. Which settings should you configure?
options: Enable reviewer decision helpers only
Enable auto-apply results and set 'If reviewers don't respond' to Remove access
Set recurrence to weekly
Use self-review with justification required
questions.explain: Auto-apply enforces deny decisions when the review ends, and setting non-response to Remove access prevents unreviewed access from persisting. Decision helpers only advise reviewers, more frequent reviews don't enforce anything, and self-review lets users approve themselves.

questions.stem: Put the steps for running a recurring guest access review of Microsoft Teams in order.
options: Scope the review to guest users in Microsoft 365 groups and Teams
Choose reviewers, such as team owners, and set the recurrence
Configure completion settings: auto-apply results and the action for non-responses
Reviewers record approve or deny decisions during the review period
Results are applied and review history is kept as audit evidence
questions.explain: Define scope first, then reviewers and schedule, then completion behaviour. Reviewers decide during the instance, and at the end results are applied (removing denied guests) with history retained for auditors.

questions.case: Datum Corp wants a review that asks only about users who haven't signed in for 90 days, across all its Microsoft 365 groups, with machine-learning recommendations for reviewers. It currently holds Microsoft Entra ID P2.
questions.stem: What should you tell Datum?
options: P2 already includes both capabilities
The review can only target Azure resource roles
Inactive-user-only scoping and ML-assisted recommendations require Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Datum must use Defender for Cloud Apps instead of access reviews
questions.explain: Reviews scoped only to inactive users and machine-learning-assisted recommendations are Entra ID Governance capabilities; P2 includes core reviews and inactive-user decision helpers within reviews of all users. Access reviews do cover Microsoft 365 groups, and Defender for Cloud Apps doesn't run access attestations.

questions.stem: Which THREE characteristics belong to Microsoft's privileged (PAW) device security profile? Select THREE.
options: Email and general web browsing are blocked
Application control is enforced and apps are deployed only through Intune
Users have no local administrator rights
Personal devices can be enrolled to reduce hardware costs
Outlook is allowed so admins can receive alerts
questions.explain: PAWs block email and browsing, enforce application control with Intune-deployed apps, and remove local admin rights. BYOD isn't allowed for PAWs, and allowing Outlook would describe the specialized profile, not privileged.

questions.stem: Global Administrators must be able to use their role only from PAWs, which are tagged with extensionAttribute1 = 'PAW' in Microsoft Entra ID. How should you enforce this?
options: A named location for the admins' home IP addresses
An Intune compliance policy assigned to all devices
An access review of Global Administrators
A CA policy for directory roles blocking devices that don't match a device filter on extensionAttribute1
questions.explain: A CA filter for devices can target or exclude devices by extensionAttribute values, so admins are blocked from any device that isn't a PAW. Home IPs don't identify devices, a general compliance policy would let any compliant laptop pass, and access reviews don't control device use.

questions.stem: You must stop exposing RDP and SSH on Azure VMs to the internet. Admins should connect over TLS from the Azure portal, VMs must have no public IPs, and sessions must be recorded. What should you recommend?
options: Azure Bastion Premium
Just-in-time VM access only
Azure Firewall DNAT rules for port 3389
Azure Bastion Developer
questions.explain: Azure Bastion brokers RDP/SSH over TLS 443 to VMs without public IPs, and the Premium SKU adds session recording. JIT still opens management ports to the requester's IP, Firewall DNAT publishes RDP to the internet, and the Developer SKU lacks advanced features like recording.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan is needed to use just-in-time (JIT) VM access?
options: Defender for Servers Plan 1
Foundational CSPM (free)
Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender for Storage
questions.explain: JIT VM access is a Defender for Servers Plan 2 feature, alongside capabilities such as file integrity monitoring. Plan 1 focuses on Defender for Endpoint integration, foundational CSPM is posture only, and Defender for Storage protects storage accounts.

questions.stem: A regulation requires that customer data for EU citizens is stored only in EU regions. Which control best translates this requirement into an enforceable technical control in Azure?
options: A Defender for Cloud Secure Score recommendation
An Azure Policy 'Allowed locations' assignment with deny effect at the EU management group
A sensitivity label named 'EU data'
A Compliance Manager improvement action assigned to the CISO
questions.explain: Allowed locations with deny blocks resource creation outside the listed regions, which is testable and enforced. Secure Score recommendations and improvement actions track work but don't block anything, and a sensitivity label classifies content without restricting where Azure resources are deployed.

questions.stem: For each statement about compliance and the shared responsibility model, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Physical datacenter security is a Microsoft-managed control for Azure services.
Because Microsoft Azure holds ISO 27001 certification, a customer's workloads are automatically ISO 27001 compliant.
The Microsoft cloud security benchmark maps its controls to frameworks such as CIS, NIST and PCI DSS.

questions.explain: Microsoft manages physical security. Microsoft's certifications cover its responsibilities only; customer-managed controls must be implemented and evidenced. MCSB maps to CIS, NIST and PCI DSS to help translate requirements into controls.

questions.case: An insurer must meet three requirements: (1) all access to claims data is logged and kept for 7 years; (2) only claims staff can open claims documents, even if files are emailed externally; (3) databases use keys the insurer controls.
questions.stem: Which THREE controls map to these requirements? Select THREE.
options: Purview Audit (Premium) with the 10-year retention add-on and a matching audit retention policy
Sensitivity labels with encryption restricting access to claims staff
Transparent data encryption with customer-managed keys in Key Vault
Azure DDoS Protection on the claims virtual network
Defender for Cloud Secure Score
questions.explain: Long-term audit retention meets requirement 1, label-based encryption travels with the file for requirement 2, and TDE with customer-managed keys meets requirement 3. DDoS Protection addresses availability, and Secure Score measures posture; neither satisfies these specific obligations.

questions.stem: A compliance officer wants to track the organization's progress against ISO 27001, assign tasks to control owners, upload evidence, and see which controls Microsoft already manages. Which tool should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Secure Score
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium)
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Microsoft Service Trust Portal
questions.explain: Compliance Manager provides ISO 27001 assessments with Microsoft-managed, customer-managed and shared controls, assignable improvement actions with evidence, and a compliance score. Secure Score tracks security posture, eDiscovery supports legal investigations, and the Service Trust Portal publishes Microsoft's own audit reports.

questions.stem: Financial records in SharePoint must be kept for 7 years, be unchangeable during that period, and require a reviewer's approval before deletion. Which Purview capability fits?
options: A retention label that declares items as records with disposition review
A DLP policy for SharePoint
An Audit (Premium) retention policy
A sensitivity label with encryption
questions.explain: Records management retention labels can retain content for 7 years, mark it as a record to lock edits and deletion, and require disposition review at the end. DLP prevents sharing, audit retention keeps activity logs rather than documents, and sensitivity labels protect confidentiality, not retention.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Assessments can be created from regulatory templates such as ISO 27001 or NIST.
A high compliance score certifies that the organization is compliant with a regulation.
Assessments include Microsoft-managed, customer-managed and shared controls.

questions.explain: Compliance Manager builds assessments from 360+ templates and categorises controls by responsibility. The compliance score measures progress on improvement actions; it doesn't replace an auditor's certification.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure Policy rule so that creation of storage accounts that allow public network access is blocked.
options: "audit"
"deny"
"auditIfNotExists"
"disabled"
questions.explain: The deny effect blocks non-compliant create and update requests. Audit and auditIfNotExists only report non-compliance, and disabled turns the rule off.

questions.case: Contoso assigned a deployIfNotExists policy at the Landing Zones management group that configures diagnostic settings on Key Vaults to send logs to the central Sentinel workspace. New vaults comply, but 120 existing vaults still show as non-compliant a week later.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Change the effect to deny
Create a policy exemption for the existing vaults
Reassign the policy at each subscription
Create a remediation task for the assignment, using its managed identity
questions.explain: DINE applies automatically only to new or updated resources; existing ones need a remediation task, which runs with the assignment's managed identity. Deny would block changes rather than fix vaults, an exemption hides the gap, and reassigning at lower scopes doesn't remediate existing resources.

questions.stem: A company uses only the free foundational CSPM capabilities of Defender for Cloud and wants to show PCI DSS v4 compliance in the regulatory compliance dashboard. What is required?
options: Nothing; all standards are available for free
Enable at least one eligible paid Defender plan, such as Defender CSPM, and add the PCI DSS standard
Purchase Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager premium templates
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 only
questions.explain: Only MCSB is shown by default; adding other regulatory standards requires a paid Defender plan (any except Defender for Servers Plan 1 or Defender for APIs Plan 1), and custom standards require Defender CSPM. Compliance Manager templates are a separate Purview tool.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Controls that can't be assessed automatically appear as not available and can be manually attested.
The Microsoft cloud security benchmark can assess AWS and GCP resources as well as Azure.
A fully green dashboard is equivalent to passing an external PCI DSS audit.

questions.explain: Procedural or platform-owned controls show as not available and can be attested manually. MCSB applies across Azure, AWS and GCP. The dashboard reflects automated assessments and attestations; it supports but does not replace an external audit.

questions.stem: Which Azure Policy effects require a managed identity on the policy assignment so that Azure Policy can change resources?
options: audit and deny
deployIfNotExists and modify
auditIfNotExists and disabled
append and manual
questions.explain: deployIfNotExists deploys related resources and modify changes properties such as tags, so both need a managed identity with suitable RBAC roles. Audit, deny, auditIfNotExists, disabled and manual don't change resources; append alters the request inline without needing an identity.

questions.stem: You are designing Azure Policy governance for an Azure landing zone with 60 subscriptions. Which TWO practices should you recommend? Select TWO.
options: Assign security initiatives at management group scope so new subscriptions inherit them
Roll out new guardrails with audit first, then switch to deny once impact is understood
Assign every policy separately at each resource group
Use permanent exemptions for any team that reports a failure
Disable the Microsoft cloud security benchmark initiative to reduce noise
questions.explain: Management group assignment gives consistent inherited guardrails, and audit-then-deny avoids breaking deployments. Per-resource-group assignment doesn't scale, blanket permanent exemptions erode compliance (use time-bound waivers), and MCSB is the baseline that Defender for Cloud uses.

questions.case: Margie's Travel is audited quarterly against ISO 27001. Auditors want a monthly history of control status from Defender for Cloud across Azure and AWS, kept in the central Log Analytics workspace so it can be charted and retained for two years.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Download the PDF compliance report manually each month
Enable continuous export of regulatory compliance data to the Log Analytics workspace
Create a Compliance Manager assessment and export its score
Configure Purview Audit (Premium) for Defender for Cloud
questions.explain: Continuous export streams regulatory compliance assessments (and recommendations and alerts) to Log Analytics, where they can be queried, charted in workbooks and retained. Manual PDFs aren't queryable history, Compliance Manager scores are a different data set, and Purview Audit records Microsoft 365 activity rather than Defender for Cloud control state.

questions.stem: A company must find and classify personal data stored in Azure SQL databases, Azure Storage, on-premises SQL Server and Amazon S3, to support a GDPR records-of-processing requirement. Which Microsoft Purview capability should you use?
options: Purview Data Map scanning with classification
Purview Communication Compliance
Purview Insider Risk Management
Purview eDiscovery (Standard)
questions.explain: The Purview Data Map scans registered sources across Azure, on-premises and multicloud and applies classifications such as personal data types. Communication Compliance reviews messages for conduct, Insider Risk Management correlates risky user activity, and eDiscovery collects content for legal cases.

questions.stem: You enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud on a new Azure subscription. Which standard is assigned by default and drives the security recommendations and secure score?
options: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB)
CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
ISO/IEC 27001
questions.explain: MCSB is the default standard in Defender for Cloud; its policies generate recommendations and secure score. CIS, NIST and ISO standards can be added to the regulatory compliance dashboard but are not the default.

questions.stem: Auditors need PCI DSS compliance evidence for resources in Azure and in connected AWS accounts, in addition to MCSB. What should you recommend?
options: Assign the MCSB initiative a second time with PCI DSS parameters
Enable Defender CSPM and add the PCI DSS standard in the regulatory compliance dashboard
Create a custom Microsoft Secure Score recommended action for PCI DSS
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 on the AWS connector
questions.explain: Additional regulatory standards such as PCI DSS are added in the regulatory compliance dashboard, which needs a paid plan such as Defender CSPM and works for connected AWS accounts. MCSB cannot be re-parameterised into PCI DSS, Secure Score has no custom PCI action, and Servers Plan 1 adds EDR, not compliance standards.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark, select Yes if true.

statements.s: MCSB includes security guidance for AWS and GCP as well as Azure.
An Azure service security baseline applies MCSB controls to one specific Azure service.
MCSB is a regulatory standard published by NIST.

questions.explain: MCSB is Microsoft-authored, multicloud, and mapped to frameworks such as CIS, NIST and PCI-DSS; it is not a NIST publication. Per-service security baselines apply MCSB controls to individual Azure services.

questions.stem: Your organization uses a non-Microsoft email security gateway that fully implements a Microsoft Secure Score recommended action. Which status should you set so the action's points are counted?
options: Risk accepted
Planned
Resolved through third party
To address
questions.explain: 'Resolved through third party' (like 'Resolved through alternate mitigation') awards the action's points. 'Risk accepted' gives no points, 'Planned' only affects the projected planned score, and 'To address' means work is still outstanding.

questions.stem: A Microsoft Secure Score recommended action that awards partial points by coverage is worth 9 points. 300 of your 900 users currently meet the requirement. How many points do you earn for this action?
questions.explain: Coverage-based actions award points in proportion to coverage: 300/900 x 9 = 3. Zero would apply only to binary actions not yet complete, and 9 needs full coverage.

questions.stem: For each statement about the classic secure score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud, select Yes if true.

statements.s: You must remediate every recommendation in a security control for a resource to earn that control's points.
Preview recommendations are included in the secure score calculation.
The classic secure score and the risk-based Cloud Secure Score produce directly comparable values.

questions.explain: Classic secure score awards a control's points only when all its recommendations are fixed, and excludes preview recommendations until GA. The risk-based Cloud Secure Score uses a different calculation, so the two scores are not comparable.

questions.case: Contoso runs workloads in Azure and AWS. The CISO complains that the current posture number treats a misconfigured test VM the same as an internet-facing database containing customer data. She wants a 0-100 cloud posture score that weights findings by internet exposure, data sensitivity and how critical each asset is to the business.
questions.stem: Which score should you recommend that the CISO track?
options: Cloud Secure Score in Microsoft Security Exposure Management
Classic secure score in Defender for Cloud
The Identity category of Microsoft Secure Score
Compliance score in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
questions.explain: The risk-based Cloud Secure Score weights recommendations by risk level, asset risk factors such as internet exposure and data sensitivity, and asset criticality. The classic score ignores risk factors, the Identity category covers Entra settings, and Compliance Manager measures regulatory control progress.

questions.stem: A company has 140 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations and creates new accounts every month. You must bring all of them into Defender for Cloud with the least ongoing administrative effort. What should you do?
options: Create a single-account connector for each AWS account by using Terraform
Create a connector for the AWS management account so member and new accounts are provisioned automatically
Create a connector for an AWS delegated administrator account
Install the Azure Arc agent on every EC2 instance instead of using connectors
questions.explain: A management account connector auto-provisions connectors for existing and newly created member accounts. Per-account connectors require ongoing work, delegated administrator accounts are not supported for this, and Arc alone covers servers but not AWS service posture.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities are included in the free Foundational CSPM tier of Defender for Cloud? Select TWO.
options: Secure score
Security recommendations based on MCSB
Attack path analysis
Agentless VM vulnerability scanning
Governance rules
questions.explain: Foundational CSPM includes asset inventory, MCSB recommendations, secure score and remediation tools. Attack path analysis, agentless VM scanning and governance rules are Defender CSPM (paid) features.

questions.case: Fabrikam deploys infrastructure from Terraform stored in GitHub to Azure and GCP. Security wants a misconfiguration found in a running cloud resource to be traced back to the exact IaC file and repository that created it, and wants to see whether that resource lies on an exploitable path to sensitive data.
questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud plan meets both requirements?
options: Foundational CSPM with a GitHub connector
Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender CSPM
Defender for Containers
questions.explain: Code-to-cloud contextualization and attack path analysis both require Defender CSPM. Foundational CSPM with a DevOps connector gives only basic DevOps recommendations, and the Servers and Containers plans protect workloads rather than map code to cloud.

questions.stem: You are connecting an AWS account to Defender for Cloud. Put the steps in order.
options: In Defender for Cloud environment settings, add an AWS environment and enter the account details
Select the Defender plans to enable on the connector
Choose the deployment method and obtain the CloudFormation template
Run the template in AWS to create the IAM roles trusted by Defender for Cloud
Review AWS recommendations once assessments arrive
questions.explain: The connector wizard collects account details, then plan selection, then generates the CloudFormation (or Terraform) template. Running it in AWS creates the federated IAM roles; only after that do assessments and recommendations appear.

questions.stem: Azure VMs that process card payments need file integrity monitoring and just-in-time VM access. Which plan provides both?
options: Defender for Servers Plan 1
Foundational CSPM
Defender CSPM
Defender for Servers Plan 2
questions.explain: FIM and JIT VM access are Defender for Servers Plan 2 features. Plan 1 focuses on Defender for Endpoint EDR, and the CSPM tiers provide posture rather than these workload controls.

questions.stem: Production servers are in subscription Prod and need FIM and agentless malware scanning. Lab servers are in subscription Lab and need only EDR at the lowest cost. What should you configure?
options: Plan 2 on Prod and Plan 1 on Lab
Plan 2 on both subscriptions and disable FIM on Lab
Plan 1 on both subscriptions and add FIM through Azure Policy
Defender CSPM on Prod and Foundational CSPM on Lab
questions.explain: Plan 2 adds FIM and agentless scanning for Prod, while Plan 1 delivers Defender for Endpoint EDR at lower cost for Lab. Plan 2 everywhere overspends, Plan 1 lacks FIM, and CSPM plans do not provide EDR.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Servers, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Plan 1 can be enabled on individual machines rather than the whole subscription.
Plan 2 can be enabled on individual machines rather than the whole subscription.
Plan 2 includes a free allowance of 500 MB per node per day for specific security tables in Log Analytics.

questions.explain: Plan 1 supports per-resource enablement; Plan 2 can be enabled at subscription level and only disabled per resource. Plan 2 includes a pooled 500 MB/node/day ingestion benefit for tables such as SecurityEvent.

questions.stem: You must detect malware uploaded to blob containers and alert on unusual access attempts against secrets in vaults. Which TWO Defender plans should you enable? Select TWO.
options: Defender for Storage
Defender for Key Vault
Defender for Resource Manager
Defender for App Service
Defender CSPM
questions.explain: Defender for Storage provides malware scanning and storage threat detection; Defender for Key Vault alerts on unusual vault access. Resource Manager covers control-plane operations, App Service covers web apps, and Defender CSPM is posture only.

questions.stem: SQL Server 2019 runs on on-premises Hyper-V VMs. You need vulnerability assessment and threat detection for those databases in Defender for Cloud. What should you recommend?
options: Enable Defender for Azure SQL Databases
Arc-enable the servers and enable Defender for SQL servers on machines
Enable Defender for open-source relational databases
Enable Defender for Storage on the database backup account
questions.explain: SQL Server outside Azure is protected by the SQL servers on machines plan once the hosts are Arc-enabled. The Azure SQL plan covers PaaS databases, the open-source plan covers PostgreSQL and MySQL, and Defender for Storage protects storage accounts.

questions.stem: Which Defender plan alerts when an unusual IP address performs a burst of resource deletions through Azure Resource Manager?
options: Defender for Key Vault
Defender for DNS
Defender for Resource Manager
Defender CSPM
questions.explain: Defender for Resource Manager monitors management (control-plane) operations for suspicious activity. Key Vault covers vault access, DNS covers anomalous DNS queries, and Defender CSPM provides posture rather than activity alerts.

questions.stem: Which component must be installed on an on-premises Linux server so it appears as an Azure resource that Azure Policy and Defender for Cloud can manage?
options: Azure Monitor Agent
Log Analytics agent
Azure VM Guest Agent
Azure Connected Machine agent
questions.explain: The Connected Machine agent registers the machine as an Azure Arc-enabled server with a resource ID. Azure Monitor Agent only collects telemetry, the Log Analytics agent is retired, and the VM Guest Agent exists only on Azure VMs.

questions.stem: Servers in a colocation datacenter will be Azure Arc-enabled. Which THREE capabilities does this make available for them? Select THREE.
options: Auditing OS settings with Azure Policy machine configuration
Protection by Defender for Servers
Patching through Azure Update Manager
Automatic live migration of the servers into Azure
Access through Azure DNS private resolver without network connectivity
questions.explain: Arc projects the servers into Azure Resource Manager so machine configuration, Defender for Servers and Update Manager can manage them. Arc does not migrate servers, and it does not provide network or DNS connectivity.

questions.stem: You need an Azure Resource Graph query that lists all Azure Arc-enabled servers with their location and operating system. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where type == "microsoft.hybridcompute/machines"
| project name, location, osName = tostring(properties.osName)
options: resources
securityresources
Heartbeat
advisorresources
questions.explain: Arc-enabled servers are ARM resources of type microsoft.hybridcompute/machines in the Resource Graph resources table. securityresources holds Defender for Cloud data, Heartbeat is a Log Analytics table, and advisorresources holds Advisor recommendations.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank has 600 servers on-premises and 200 EC2 instances in AWS. All servers must be covered by Defender for Servers Plan 2 and audited with Azure Policy machine configuration. The security policy forbids the on-premises servers from sending management traffic over the public internet; an ExpressRoute circuit to Azure exists.
questions.stem: What should you include in the design for the on-premises servers?
options: Azure Arc-enabled servers with virtual network service endpoints for Microsoft.HybridCompute
Azure Arc-enabled servers connecting through an Azure Arc Private Link Scope over ExpressRoute
Defender for Endpoint installed directly with no Arc agent, reporting through Azure Bastion
Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection endpoint and no Arc registration
questions.explain: Arc is required for machine configuration and full Defender for Servers coverage, and an Arc Private Link Scope lets agents use private endpoints over ExpressRoute. Service endpoints apply only to Azure VNet traffic, Bastion is a remote-access service, and AMA alone does not create an Azure resource for Policy.

questions.stem: In Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management, what do you supply so the service can start discovering your internet-facing infrastructure?
options: An Azure Arc agent on each public web server
A Defender for Cloud AWS connector
Discovery seeds such as known domains and IP blocks
A Log Analytics data connection
questions.explain: Defender EASM recursively discovers related assets starting from discovery seeds. It is agentless and outside-in, so Arc agents and cloud connectors are not needed, and data connections only export findings.

questions.stem: Defender EASM discovers a host that has some relationship to your seeds but not a strong enough connection to confirm ownership. In which inventory state does it appear for manual review?
options: Approved Inventory
Dependency
Monitor Only
Candidate
questions.explain: Candidate assets are related to seeds but need manual review to confirm ownership. Approved Inventory is confirmed as owned, Dependency is third-party infrastructure you rely on, and Monitor Only is relevant but not under your control.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender EASM, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Websites run by franchisees that matter to your brand but are not under your control are best labelled Monitor Only.
A managed service provider can operate a customer's Defender EASM resource through Azure Lighthouse.
Discovered asset types include domains, IP address blocks, hosts, ASNs and Whois organizations.

questions.explain: Monitor Only suits related but uncontrolled assets. Defender EASM does not support cross-tenant access, including Azure Lighthouse, so users must authenticate to the resource's tenant. The listed asset types are all discovered.

questions.stem: Attack path analysis shows no results for your Azure VMs. Which configuration is required for VM-based attack paths?
options: Defender CSPM plus agentless scanning for VMs or Defender for Servers vulnerability assessment
Foundational CSPM plus Azure Arc on every VM
Defender for Servers Plan 1 only
Microsoft Sentinel with UEBA enabled
questions.explain: Attack path analysis requires Defender CSPM together with vulnerability data from agentless VM scanning or Defender for Servers. Foundational CSPM does not include attack paths, Arc is not needed for Azure VMs, and Sentinel UEBA is unrelated.

questions.stem: A threat analyst wants to run an ad hoc query to find internet-exposed VMs that have high-severity vulnerabilities and whose managed identities can access a key vault. Which tool should the analyst use?
options: Attack path analysis
Cloud security explorer
The regulatory compliance dashboard
Workflow automation
questions.explain: Cloud security explorer builds custom graph queries across exposure, vulnerabilities and permissions. Attack path analysis shows prebuilt paths that Microsoft computes, the compliance dashboard tracks standards, and workflow automation triggers Logic Apps.

questions.stem: Put the elements of a typical Defender CSPM attack path in order, from where the attacker starts to what they reach.
options: Internet-exposed VM with an exploitable vulnerability
Managed identity attached to the VM
Role assignment granting that identity data access
Storage account containing sensitive data
questions.explain: Attack paths begin at an exploitable entry point, move laterally through identities and permissions, and end at a critical target such as sensitive data. Breaking any link, for example the role assignment, breaks the path.

questions.stem: Leadership wants one scored programme that tracks readiness against ransomware across endpoints, identities and cloud, with metrics and prioritised recommendations, reviewed monthly. What should you use?
options: Microsoft Secure Score history for the Apps category
A Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager assessment
The Ransomware Protection security initiative in Microsoft Security Exposure Management
The Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard
questions.explain: Exposure Management security initiatives such as Ransomware Protection give scored, cross-domain metrics and recommendations for a threat. Secure Score categories are not threat-specific, Compliance Manager tracks regulations, and the compliance dashboard tracks cloud standards.

questions.stem: You are planning the rollout of attack surface reduction rules in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Which THREE modes can a rule be set to? Select THREE.
options: Audit
Block
Warn
Quarantine
Learn
questions.explain: ASR rules can be set to Audit, Block or Warn (or left not configured/disabled). Quarantine is an antivirus remediation action and Learn is not an ASR mode. Best practice is to start in Audit before moving to Block.

questions.stem: You need an Azure Resource Graph query that returns the Defender for Cloud secure score percentage for each subscription. Complete the query.
questions.code:
securityresources
| where type == "____"
| extend percentage = properties.score.percentage
| project subscriptionId, percentage
options: microsoft.security/assessments
microsoft.security/pricings
microsoft.security/regulatorycompliancestandards
microsoft.security/securescores
questions.explain: Secure score records are of type microsoft.security/securescores and expose properties.score.percentage. Assessments are individual recommendation results, pricings are the plan settings, and regulatorycompliancestandards hold compliance state.

questions.stem: Your server standard states that no Azure VM may expose RDP or SSH to the internet, yet administrators must still be able to connect from the Azure portal over TLS without a VPN. What should you include?
options: Azure Bastion
A public IP with an NSG rule allowing TCP 3389 from Any
Azure Front Door
Azure Application Gateway
questions.explain: Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH over TLS to VMs with no public IPs. Opening 3389 to Any violates the standard, and Front Door and Application Gateway are HTTP(S) load balancers, not admin access services.

questions.stem: You are writing security requirements for Linux VMs in Azure. Which TWO requirements reduce credential theft risk for administrative sign-in? Select TWO.
options: Use Microsoft Entra ID login for Linux with Azure RBAC roles
Use SSH key authentication and disable password authentication
Use the same local root password on all VMs for break-glass access
Allow SSH from the internet but change the port to 2222
Store SSH private keys in the VM's custom data
questions.explain: Entra ID login applies RBAC and Conditional Access, and SSH keys remove password guessing. A shared root password enables lateral movement, moving the port is obscurity not control, and custom data is readable metadata, not a secret store.

questions.case: Litware runs Windows Server and Red Hat Linux servers in Azure, in AWS EC2 and in two on-premises datacenters. The architecture board wants a single requirement that guarantees all servers receive EDR, appear in one posture score, and can be audited against an OS baseline using the same tooling regardless of location.
questions.stem: What should you specify?
options: Install Defender for Endpoint manually on every server and track posture in a spreadsheet
Arc for all non-Azure servers, plus Defender for Servers and machine configuration at management group scope
Defender for Servers Plan 1 on Azure subscriptions only, and AWS Inspector for EC2
Microsoft Intune enrolment for all servers with the Windows security baseline
questions.explain: Arc brings non-Azure servers into Azure Resource Manager so Defender for Servers and machine configuration apply uniformly, and management group scope covers new subscriptions. Manual onboarding gives no unified posture, splitting tools breaks consistency, and Intune baselines target clients, not Linux servers.

questions.stem: Contractors use personal Android phones and refuse to enrol them in Intune. You must stop corporate email data being copied into personal apps and be able to remove only corporate data. What should you recommend?
options: An Intune device compliance policy with 'Require device to be marked as compliant'
Android Enterprise fully managed enrolment
An Intune app protection policy, enforced with the Conditional Access grant 'Require app protection policy'
A Conditional Access policy that blocks all Android platforms
questions.explain: App protection (MAM) policies work without enrolment, restrict data transfer and support selective wipe; Conditional Access enforces them. Compliance requires enrolment, fully managed is for corporate devices, and blocking Android stops the work entirely.

questions.stem: For each statement about mobile device security, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on iOS and Android can detect phishing websites and report a device risk level to Intune.
A selective wipe removes all personal photos and apps from a BYOD phone.
Intune compliance policies can mark jailbroken or rooted devices as noncompliant.

questions.explain: Defender for Endpoint mobile provides web protection and a risk signal usable in compliance. Selective wipe removes only corporate app data. Compliance policies include jailbreak/root detection.

questions.case: Tailspin issues corporate iPhones to executives and allows staff to use personal phones for Teams. After a phishing incident, the CISO wants corporate phones that visit malicious sites to lose access to Microsoft 365 automatically until the threat is cleared, without affecting personal phones' privacy.
questions.stem: Which design meets the requirement for the corporate iPhones?
options: Require an app protection policy in Conditional Access for all phones
Create a sign-in risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection that blocks medium risk
Apply an app protection policy that requires a six-digit PIN
Defender for Endpoint on iOS feeding an Intune device threat level compliance rule, plus CA requiring compliance
questions.explain: Defender for Endpoint's device threat level feeds an Intune compliance rule, and Conditional Access then blocks noncompliant devices until the threat clears. App protection policies and PINs do not react to device threats, and sign-in risk evaluates the authentication, not device compromise.

questions.stem: A manufacturer will ship 50,000 connected devices that report to Azure IoT Hub. Which identity design should you require?
options: A unique X.509 certificate per device, hardware-protected and enrolled through Device Provisioning Service
One shared access signature key embedded in the firmware of every device
A single Microsoft Entra service principal shared by all devices
Device authentication disabled, relying on an IP filter on the IoT hub
questions.explain: Per-device X.509 identity with hardware-protected keys and DPS supports secure, revocable, zero-touch enrolment. A shared key or service principal lets one compromised device impersonate the fleet, and IP filtering is not authentication.

questions.stem: Office printers, VoIP phones and conference room displays cannot run security agents. Which TWO requirements should you specify? Select TWO.
options: Discover and assess the devices agentlessly with Defender for IoT Enterprise IoT through Defender for Endpoint
Place the devices in a segmented network that allows only required flows
Install the Defender for IoT micro agent on each device as the long-term standard
Run Defender for Servers Plan 2 on each device
Allow the devices inbound access from the internet for vendor support
questions.explain: Enterprise IoT discovery through Defender for Endpoint and network segmentation suit agentless devices. The micro agent is scheduled to retire in June 2027 and needs device builder integration, Defender for Servers is for servers, and inbound internet access increases exposure.

questions.stem: How do Microsoft Defender for IoT OT network sensors usually receive the traffic they analyse?
options: From an agent installed on each PLC
From a SPAN (mirror) port or network TAP
From active scanning of every IP in the OT subnet
From Windows event forwarding on HMI workstations
questions.explain: OT sensors passively receive mirrored traffic from a SPAN port or TAP and apply deep packet inspection. Agents on PLCs are not possible, active scanning risks disrupting OT, and event forwarding is not the sensor's data source.

questions.case: A power generation company must monitor ICS networks at a plant that, by regulation, has no connection to the internet or to Azure. The SOC must still see alerts in its on-premises SIEM, and the security team will update threat intelligence during monthly maintenance windows.
questions.stem: Which Defender for IoT design should you recommend?
options: Cloud-connected OT sensors sending alerts to Microsoft Sentinel
Deploy the legacy on-premises management console to aggregate sensors
Locally managed OT sensors, manual threat intelligence updates, alerts forwarded to the on-premises SIEM
Defender for Endpoint on each HMI with Enterprise IoT discovery
questions.explain: Locally managed sensors keep all data on-premises, support manual threat intelligence updates and can forward alerts to partner systems. Cloud-connected sensors need Azure connectivity, the on-premises management console is retired, and endpoint agents do not cover ICS protocol traffic.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for IoT in OT environments, select Yes if true.

statements.s: OT sensors process and analyse traffic locally and send only telemetry and insights to the cloud.
A policy violation alert is raised when traffic deviates from the learned or configured baseline.
Cloud-connected sensors require threat intelligence packages to be uploaded manually.

questions.explain: Sensors analyse on the box, which suits low-bandwidth sites. The policy violation engine detects deviations from the baseline. Cloud-connected sensors receive threat intelligence automatically; manual upload applies to locally managed sensors.

questions.stem: You are deploying a cloud-connected Defender for IoT OT sensor at a factory. Put the steps in order.
options: Map the OT network and choose the switches to mirror
Configure a SPAN port or install a TAP on the selected switch
Onboard the sensor in the Azure portal and download its activation file
Upload the activation file in the installed sensor's console
Review the device inventory and baseline during the learning period
questions.explain: Plan traffic sources, provide mirrored traffic, onboard in Azure to obtain the activation file, activate the sensor with it, and finally review inventory while the sensor learns the baseline.

questions.stem: Which Security Compliance Toolkit component compares sets of Group Policy Objects against a baseline and highlights conflicting or redundant settings?
options: LGPO
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
Intune Settings catalog
Policy Analyzer
questions.explain: Policy Analyzer compares GPO sets and flags conflicts. LGPO applies policy to a local machine, Defender Vulnerability Management assesses vulnerabilities and configuration, and the Settings catalog is an Intune profile type.

questions.stem: Windows Server machines in an on-premises datacenter are Azure Arc-enabled but not managed by Intune. You must continuously audit them against the Microsoft-recommended Windows OS baseline and show results in Defender for Cloud. What should you use?
options: Azure Policy machine configuration with the Azure compute security baseline
An Intune Windows security baseline profile
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Azure Automation State Configuration
questions.explain: Machine configuration audits Azure and Arc-enabled servers against the compute security baseline, and results appear as Defender for Cloud recommendations. Intune baselines require Intune management, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and machine configuration is the recommended successor to Automation State Configuration.

questions.stem: For each statement about Intune security baselines, select Yes if true.

statements.s: When a new baseline version is released, profiles on the older version become read-only for settings until you update them.
Intune security baselines can never conflict with other Intune device configuration profiles.
Separate baselines exist for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Microsoft Edge.

questions.explain: Older baseline versions become read-only for settings; you update the profile to the new version. Baselines can conflict with other profiles that manage the same settings. Intune offers Defender for Endpoint, Edge, Windows and Microsoft 365 Apps baselines, among others.

questions.case: Adatum has Intune-managed Windows 11 laptops, AD DS-joined Windows Server 2022 file servers in a branch that will not be Arc-enabled this year, and Azure VMs. The architect must specify one baseline mechanism per platform that matches how each is managed.
questions.stem: Which TWO mechanisms should the architect specify? Select TWO.
options: Intune Windows and Defender for Endpoint security baselines for the laptops
Group Policy baselines from the Security Compliance Toolkit for the branch file servers
Intune security baselines for the AD DS-joined file servers
Azure Policy machine configuration for the branch file servers
Local Group Policy edited by hand on each laptop
questions.explain: Intune-managed laptops take Intune baselines, and AD DS-joined servers without Arc or Intune take GPO baselines from the SCT. Intune baselines need Intune management, machine configuration needs Azure or Arc, and hand-editing local policy does not scale.

questions.stem: What attack does Windows LAPS mainly mitigate?
options: Phishing of user cloud credentials
Lateral movement using a local administrator password shared across many devices
Ransomware encryption of file shares
Token replay against Microsoft Graph
questions.explain: Unique, rotated local admin passwords stop an attacker reusing one stolen local credential or hash across the estate. Phishing, ransomware encryption and token replay are addressed by other controls such as phishing-resistant MFA, backups and CAE.

questions.stem: For each statement about Windows LAPS, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device can back up its password to both Entra ID and Active Directory at the same time.
Windows LAPS can back up the DSRM account password of domain controllers to Active Directory.
Password encryption in Active Directory requires the Windows Server 2016 domain functional level or later.

questions.explain: Hybrid-joined devices choose one backup target, not both. DSRM password backup is supported for domain controllers to AD (with encryption). AD password encryption requires the Windows Server 2016 domain functional level.

questions.stem: A helpdesk lead must retrieve the current Windows LAPS password for an Entra-joined device from PowerShell. Complete the command.
questions.code:
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Device.Read.All","DeviceLocalCredential.Read.All"
____ -DeviceIds "LAPTOP-0042" -IncludePasswords -AsPlainText
options: Get-LapsADPassword
Reset-LapsPassword
Get-LapsAADPassword
Get-LapsDiagnostics
questions.explain: Get-LapsAADPassword queries passwords backed up to Microsoft Entra ID through Microsoft Graph. Get-LapsADPassword reads from Active Directory, Reset-LapsPassword rotates on the local device, and Get-LapsDiagnostics collects troubleshooting logs.

questions.case: Northwind uses legacy Microsoft LAPS (MSI) on AD DS-joined servers and stores passwords in clear text attributes. Auditors require that LAPS passwords be encrypted at rest in the directory, that previous passwords be recoverable after a server image rollback, and that the old MSI be removed. Domain functional level is Windows Server 2016.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Keep legacy LAPS and enable legacy LAPS emulation mode
Back up the passwords to Microsoft Entra ID using Intune
Enable BitLocker on domain controllers to encrypt the AD database
Migrate to native Windows LAPS with AD backup, password encryption and encrypted password history enabled
questions.explain: Native Windows LAPS supports AD password encryption and encrypted history at the 2016 functional level. Emulation mode stores passwords in clear text without history, AD-joined servers cannot back up to Entra ID, and BitLocker protects disks, not attribute access.

questions.stem: Your helpdesk needs to read LAPS passwords for Entra-joined devices, but you must avoid granting Intune Administrator or Cloud Device Administrator. What should you do?
options: Create a custom Microsoft Entra role with the device local credential password read permission and assign it
Assign the Global Reader role
Assign the Helpdesk Administrator role
Grant the helpdesk group Read access on the computer objects in AD
questions.explain: A custom role with the device local credential password read permission gives least privilege. Global Reader and Helpdesk Administrator do not read LAPS passwords, and AD ACLs do not apply to passwords stored in Entra ID.

questions.stem: Which Azure service enables zero-touch, just-in-time enrolment of large numbers of IoT devices into the correct IoT hub using per-device attestation?
options: Azure Arc-enabled servers
Azure IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service
Microsoft Intune Autopilot
Azure Digital Twins
questions.explain: DPS performs attestation (X.509, TPM or symmetric key) and assigns devices to IoT hubs at scale. Arc connects servers, Autopilot provisions Windows PCs, and Digital Twins models environments.

questions.stem: For an Azure SQL Database (PaaS), which layer is the customer responsible for securing?
options: Patching the underlying Windows Server operating system
Physical security of the datacenter hosts
Service configuration such as firewall rules, authentication and auditing
Hypervisor hardening
questions.explain: In PaaS, Microsoft runs the OS, hypervisor and physical layers; the customer configures the service, its network access, identities and data. OS patching, physical security and hypervisor hardening are provider duties for PaaS.

questions.stem: You must prevent anyone from creating storage accounts that allow public network access across 60 subscriptions, including future ones. What should you recommend?
options: Enable Defender for Storage on each subscription
Create a Microsoft Secure Score recommended action
Configure resource locks on each existing storage account
Assign an Azure Policy definition with the Deny effect at the root or intermediate management group
questions.explain: A Deny policy at management group scope blocks non-compliant creation and is inherited by new subscriptions. Defender for Storage detects threats but does not block configurations, Secure Score cannot enforce, and locks only stop deletion or changes to existing resources.

questions.stem: Your company uses Salesforce and ServiceNow. Security wants configuration recommendations for these SaaS apps alongside Microsoft 365 recommendations in Secure Score. What must you do first?
options: Connect each app to Defender for Cloud Apps with an app connector and turn on security recommendations
Add the apps as Defender for Cloud environment connectors
Onboard the apps to Azure Arc
Configure Global Secure Access Private Access for the apps
questions.explain: SaaS security posture management requires the app connector in Defender for Cloud Apps with security recommendations turned on; recommendations then appear in Secure Score and Exposure Management. Defender for Cloud connectors cover AWS, GCP and DevOps, Arc covers servers, and Private Access is for private apps.

questions.stem: Which TWO Azure Policy effects can automatically correct non-compliant resources rather than only report on them? Select TWO.
options: DeployIfNotExists
Modify
Audit
AuditIfNotExists
Disabled
questions.explain: DeployIfNotExists and Modify can remediate resources (with a managed identity and remediation task). Audit and AuditIfNotExists only report, and Disabled turns the policy off.

questions.stem: An Azure Function processes messages from IoT Hub by using a connection string that contains the iothubowner shared access key. What should you recommend instead?
options: Rotating the iothubowner key every 90 days
A managed identity for the function with an IoT Hub data role assigned through Azure RBAC
Storing the iothubowner key in the function's app settings in plain text
Creating a second shared access policy with registry write permissions
questions.explain: A managed identity with Entra ID RBAC removes stored secrets and grants least privilege. Rotating or relocating the owner key still uses an over-privileged shared secret, and another policy with registry write adds privilege.

questions.case: A medical device maker sends patient telemetry from 20,000 devices to Azure IoT Hub. Regulations require that the hub is not reachable from the public internet except by devices over a dedicated carrier private APN connected to Azure, that back-end services reading telemetry use no shared secrets, and that any stolen device can be cut off quickly.
questions.stem: Which THREE requirements should you include? Select THREE.
options: Private endpoints for IoT Hub with public network access disabled
Managed identities with Azure RBAC data roles for back-end services that read from the hub
Per-device identities so a single device can be disabled in IoT Hub or DPS
One group symmetric key shared by all devices
Basic tier IoT Hub to reduce attack surface
questions.explain: Private endpoints meet the network rule, managed identities with RBAC remove shared secrets from back-end services, and per-device identity allows revoking one stolen device. A shared group key cannot revoke individual devices, and the hub tier does not reduce attack surface.

questions.stem: Which service should protect a public web app from SQL injection and cross-site scripting at the HTTP layer?
options: Azure Firewall Standard
Network security groups
Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door or Application Gateway
Azure DDoS Network Protection
questions.explain: Azure WAF inspects HTTP requests with managed OWASP-based rule sets. Azure Firewall Standard filters network and FQDN traffic, NSGs filter at layers 3-4, and DDoS Protection mitigates volumetric attacks.

questions.stem: For each statement about securing Azure App Service, select Yes if true.

statements.s: HTTPS Only is enabled by default on new App Service apps.
A Key Vault reference lets an app setting resolve a secret from Key Vault by using the app's managed identity.
Basic authentication for FTP and SCM endpoints should be disabled in favour of Microsoft Entra ID-based deployment.

questions.explain: HTTPS Only must be turned on explicitly. Key Vault references use the app's managed identity to fetch secrets. Microsoft recommends disabling basic auth on FTP and SCM endpoints.

questions.stem: Your company has about 400 public IP addresses across many virtual networks and wants DDoS mitigation plus access to the DDoS Rapid Response team and cost protection for scale-out during attacks. Which option should you recommend?
options: Azure DDoS IP Protection
The default DDoS infrastructure protection only
Azure Firewall Premium with IDPS
Azure DDoS Network Protection
questions.explain: DDoS Network Protection includes rapid response support, cost protection and a WAF discount. IP Protection lacks rapid response and cost protection, default infrastructure protection is not tuned per customer, and Firewall IDPS is not DDoS mitigation.

questions.case: Proseware publishes partner APIs through Azure API Management. The security team discovered that several endpoints accept calls without any token, and some responses contain payment card data. They want an inventory of all published APIs, flagging of unauthenticated endpoints and sensitive data, and runtime detection of OWASP API Top 10 attacks.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Enable Defender for APIs in Defender for Cloud for the API Management instance
Enable Defender for App Service on the back-end web apps
Deploy Azure Firewall Premium with TLS inspection in front of API Management
Turn on Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium)
questions.explain: Defender for APIs inventories APIs in API Management, flags unauthenticated endpoints, classifies sensitive data and detects OWASP API Top 10 threats. App Service protection lacks API inventory, Firewall Premium does not classify API data, and Purview Audit records Microsoft 365 activity.

questions.stem: You are introducing Azure WAF in front of a busy production site without blocking legitimate users. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a WAF policy with the managed Default Rule Set in Detection mode
Associate the policy with the Front Door endpoint
Review WAF logs for false positives
Add exclusions or custom rules to tune the policy
Switch the policy to Prevention mode
questions.explain: Start in Detection mode, attach the policy, observe logs, tune exclusions for false positives, and only then enforce in Prevention mode so legitimate traffic is not blocked.

questions.stem: A container that has been running for weeks suddenly launches a cryptominer binary that was not in the original image. Which Defender for Containers capability detects this?
options: Agentless discovery for Kubernetes
Binary drift detection
Registry image vulnerability assessment
Control plane hardening recommendations
questions.explain: Binary drift detection alerts on (or blocks) executables that were not part of the original image. Agentless discovery inventories clusters, registry scanning finds CVEs in stored images, and control-plane recommendations assess configuration.

questions.stem: You are writing image security requirements for Azure Container Registry. Which THREE should you include? Select THREE.
options: Disable the registry admin user and grant clusters the AcrPull role
Use private endpoints and disable public network access to the registry
Continuously scan registry images for vulnerabilities with Defender for Containers
Store database passwords as environment variables in the Dockerfile
Allow anonymous pull so build agents do not need credentials
questions.explain: Entra RBAC instead of the admin user, private network access, and continuous scanning are standard requirements. Baking secrets into Dockerfiles exposes them in image layers, and anonymous pull removes access control.

questions.case: After a supply chain incident in which a tampered public image reached production, Contoso's board requires that only images built by the company's own pipeline, scanned, and cryptographically attested can run in its AKS clusters. Developers currently pull base images directly from Docker Hub at deploy time.
questions.stem: Which design best meets the requirement?
options: Enable Defender for Containers runtime alerts and keep pulling from Docker Hub
Scan the Docker Hub images once a quarter with a third-party scanner
Import base images to ACR, scan and sign in the pipeline, and admit only signed images from that registry
Use Azure Firewall to allow docker.io only during business hours
questions.explain: Bringing images into a controlled registry, scanning and signing in CI, and admitting only signed images enforces provenance. Runtime alerts detect after deployment, quarterly scans leave long gaps, and time-based firewall rules do not verify image integrity.

questions.stem: An Entra-integrated AKS cluster must stop anyone retrieving the static cluster-admin kubeconfig. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code: az aks update --resource-group rg-prod --name aks-prod ____
options: --enable-azure-rbac
--enable-private-cluster
--api-server-authorized-ip-ranges 10.0.0.0/16
--disable-local-accounts
questions.explain: --disable-local-accounts blocks static credentials, so az aks get-credentials --admin fails. Azure RBAC changes authorisation but leaves local accounts, private cluster is a create-time network setting, and authorized IP ranges restrict source addresses only.

questions.stem: Pods in AKS need to read secrets from Azure Key Vault without storing any credential in the cluster. What should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Entra Workload ID with the Secrets Store CSI driver
A Kubernetes Secret containing a service principal client secret
The cluster's kubelet identity shared by all pods
Key Vault access through a public endpoint with an access key
questions.explain: Workload ID federates a Kubernetes service account with an Entra identity, and the CSI driver mounts Key Vault secrets, so no credential is stored. A stored client secret is a credential, sharing the kubelet identity breaks least privilege, and Key Vault has no access keys.

questions.case: Fabrikam's AKS cluster hosts a payments workload. Requirements: the Kubernetes API must not be reachable from the internet; pods must not be able to run as privileged; east-west traffic between namespaces must be restricted; and all outbound internet traffic must be inspected and logged centrally.
questions.stem: Which THREE design elements should you include? Select THREE.
options: Deploy AKS as a private cluster
Enforce Pod Security Admission or the Azure Policy add-on to deny privileged pods
Apply Kubernetes network policies and route egress through Azure Firewall with a user-defined route
Expose the API server with a public IP and rely on kubeconfig secrecy
Use the default allow-all pod network and inspect traffic later in Sentinel
questions.explain: A private cluster removes public API access, admission control blocks privileged pods, and network policies plus Firewall egress meet segmentation and inspection. A public API endpoint and an allow-all pod network contradict the requirements.

questions.stem: For each statement about AKS security, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Nightly OS security patches on Linux nodes also update the node's base image, so node image upgrades are unnecessary.
Defender for Containers can protect Kubernetes clusters in AWS and GCP as well as AKS.
Kubernetes RBAC role bindings can reference Microsoft Entra groups when the cluster is Entra-integrated.

questions.explain: Nightly patches do not change the base image, so new nodes start unpatched without node image upgrades. Defender for Containers covers AKS, EKS, GKE and Arc-enabled clusters. Entra integration lets Kubernetes RBAC bind to Entra groups.

questions.stem: You must ensure an existing Azure AI services resource accepts only Microsoft Entra ID tokens, not API keys. Complete the PowerShell command.
questions.code: Set-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName "rg-ai" -Name "ai-chat" ____ $true
options: -PublicNetworkAccess
-DisableLocalAuth
-AssignIdentity
-RestrictOutboundNetworkAccess
questions.explain: -DisableLocalAuth $true turns off key-based authentication so only Entra ID works. PublicNetworkAccess controls network exposure, AssignIdentity adds a managed identity, and RestrictOutboundNetworkAccess limits egress.

questions.case: A bank launches a customer-facing generative AI assistant built on Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry. The SOC needs real-time alerts when users attempt jailbreaks or when the model may be leaking sensitive data, correlated with other incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR. The posture team separately wants to find misconfigured AI resources across subscriptions.
questions.stem: Which combination meets both needs?
options: Azure AI Content Safety only, with alerts emailed to the SOC
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager and Defender for Storage
Defender for AI Services for runtime alerts, and Defender CSPM AI security posture management for posture
Defender for App Service and Foundational CSPM
questions.explain: Defender for AI Services raises real-time AI threat alerts that flow into Defender XDR, and Defender CSPM AI-SPM finds AI misconfigurations and attack paths. Content Safety filters content but is not a SOC alerting pipeline, and the other plans do not cover AI workloads.

questions.stem: For each statement about securing Azure AI services, select Yes if true.

statements.s: After you disable local authentication, previously valid keys might be accepted for a short time while the change propagates.
A built-in Azure Policy definition can audit or enforce disabled key access across Azure AI Services resources.
Threat protection for AI services in Defender for Cloud scans image and audio tokens as well as text.

questions.explain: Disabling local auth propagates over minutes to hours, so verify with a 401 test. A built-in policy enforces key access disabled at scale. Defender for AI Services scans text tokens only.

questions.stem: An internal app built on Azure OpenAI retrieves documents from a SharePoint library and an email inbox. Attackers could hide instructions inside those documents to manipulate the model. Which control specifically addresses this?
options: Private endpoints on the Azure OpenAI resource
Customer-managed keys for the Azure OpenAI resource
Disabling local authentication on the Azure OpenAI resource
Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields for indirect (document) attacks
questions.explain: Prompt Shields detect jailbreak and indirect prompt injection hidden in grounding documents. Private endpoints, customer-managed keys and disabling keys protect network, data at rest and authentication, but not malicious instructions inside content.

questions.stem: A payment workload in Azure must have its outbound HTTPS traffic decrypted and inspected with signature-based intrusion detection and prevention. Which Azure Firewall SKU is required?
options: Premium
Standard
Basic
Standard with Firewall Manager
questions.explain: TLS inspection and signature-based IDPS are Azure Firewall Premium features. Standard provides threat intelligence and web categories, Basic targets small environments, and Firewall Manager is a management tool that does not add these features.

questions.stem: A design gives an Azure SQL Database a public endpoint protected only by its server firewall allowing the app subnet's NAT IP. Security requires the database to be reachable only from the VNet with no public exposure. What should you recommend?
options: An NSG on the app subnet that denies outbound port 1433
A private endpoint for the SQL server with a private DNS zone, and public network access disabled
Azure DDoS IP Protection on the SQL server
A user-defined route to the internet for the SQL service tag
questions.explain: A private endpoint gives the database a private IP and disabling public access removes internet exposure. Blocking 1433 breaks the app, DDoS IP Protection protects public IPs rather than removing them, and a UDR does not change the database's exposure.

questions.case: A review of Litware's Azure network finds 30 spoke VNets peered in a full mesh, each with its own NSGs and some with public IPs on VMs for remote administration. The CISO wants all traffic between spokes and to the internet inspected and logged centrally, consistent rule management, and no public management ports.
questions.stem: Which redesign should you recommend?
options: Keep the full mesh and add Azure WAF to every VNet
Replace NSGs with application security groups and keep public IPs
Hub-and-spoke with a hub Azure Firewall, UDRs, Firewall Manager policy, and Azure Bastion for admin access
Deploy a separate Azure Firewall Basic in each spoke managed individually
questions.explain: Hub-and-spoke with forced routing through a central firewall gives central inspection and logging, Firewall Manager gives consistent policy, and Bastion removes public management IPs. WAF is HTTP only, ASGs do not inspect traffic, and per-spoke firewalls fragment management.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure network security, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Application security groups let NSG rules target VMs by role instead of by IP address.
Azure Firewall Standard supports web category filtering.
Network security groups can perform TLS inspection of HTTPS traffic.

questions.explain: ASGs group NICs so rules reference roles such as web or db. Firewall Standard includes web categories. NSGs filter on IP, port and protocol only and cannot decrypt TLS.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft product provides an identity-aware secure web gateway for users' internet traffic as part of Microsoft's Security Service Edge?
options: Microsoft Entra Private Access
Azure Firewall Premium
Azure Front Door
Microsoft Entra Internet Access
questions.explain: Entra Internet Access is the SWG in Global Secure Access. Private Access is the ZTNA component for private apps, Azure Firewall protects Azure network traffic rather than roaming users, and Front Door is an inbound application delivery service.

questions.stem: The Internet Access traffic forwarding profile and client are already deployed. You need to block the gambling web category for the Sales group. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a web content filtering policy that blocks the Gambling category
Add the policy to a security profile
Create a Conditional Access policy for Sales with the session control 'Use Global Secure Access security profile'
Have a Sales user get a new token and confirm the block in the traffic logs
questions.explain: The filtering policy must exist before it can be grouped into a security profile, the profile must exist before Conditional Access can reference it, and testing requires a new token that carries the profile.

questions.case: Adatum has 40 branch offices whose devices, including shared kiosks and printers, cannot run the Global Secure Access client. Branch internet traffic must be filtered by web category through Microsoft's SSE. Head office users with the client need different, group-specific filtering.
questions.stem: How should you apply filtering to the branch traffic?
options: Connect the branches as remote networks and place the branch filtering policy in the baseline profile
Link a security profile through Conditional Access targeting the kiosk device accounts
Deploy Azure Firewall Premium in each branch
Use Private Access Quick Access with an FQDN range of *
questions.explain: Remote networks forward branch traffic without a client, and the baseline profile applies tenant-wide without Conditional Access, which suits non-user devices. CA-linked profiles depend on user tokens from the client, branch firewalls are not SSE, and Private Access is for private apps.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Microsoft Entra Internet Access are true? Select TWO.
options: Web content filtering rules can match web categories or FQDNs
TLS inspection is needed to enforce rules that depend on the full URL path or HTTP method of HTTPS traffic
It is included in every Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence at no extra cost
It requires users to connect to an on-premises VPN concentrator first
It replaces the need for Conditional Access
questions.explain: Filtering rules use categories, FQDNs or URLs, and TLS inspection is needed to see paths and methods inside HTTPS. Internet Access needs the Entra Suite or a standalone licence, does not use VPNs, and relies on Conditional Access to apply profiles.

questions.stem: Users on managed laptops must be prevented from signing in to Microsoft 365 tenants other than your own and one approved partner, including when working from home, without deploying a header-injecting proxy. What should you recommend?
options: Configure inbound cross-tenant access settings to block all external tenants
Configure tenant restrictions v2 and enable universal tenant restrictions in Global Secure Access
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks guest users
Enable source IP restoration in Global Secure Access
questions.explain: TRv2 defines allowed tenants, and universal tenant restrictions enforce it through the client without a proxy. Inbound settings control external users entering your tenant, blocking guests affects your tenant's resources, and source IP restoration only improves logging.

questions.case: Contoso's Conditional Access policies rely on a list of 200 office egress IP ranges that changes often, and an incident showed a stolen refresh token replayed from an attacker's network. Contoso has Entra ID P1 and has deployed the Global Secure Access client. It wants to block access unless traffic comes through its own SSE and to reject replayed tokens quickly.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Add the attacker's IP range to a blocked named location
Configure a GPS-based named location for all offices
Enable CA signaling and block access from any location except All Compliant Network locations
Enable tenant restrictions v2 for the Contoso tenant
questions.explain: The compliant network condition requires traffic through Contoso's own Global Secure Access, removes IP list maintenance, and blocks replayed tokens at sign-in and, for CAE apps, in near real time. Blocking one IP is reactive, GPS locations depend on the Authenticator app and do not prove the network, and TRv2 controls access to other tenants.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Global Secure Access Microsoft traffic profile, select Yes if true.

statements.s: It is included with Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
Source IP restoration lets Entra sign-in logs show the user's original public IP rather than the SSE egress IP.
A user from another tenant can satisfy your tenant's compliant network condition by using their own organisation's Global Secure Access client.

questions.explain: The Microsoft traffic profile is included in Entra ID P1/P2. Source IP restoration preserves the original IP in logs. The compliant network check is tenant-specific, so another tenant's SSE does not satisfy it.

questions.case: Fabrikam engineers from a partner company need to reach two private engineering apps in Fabrikam's datacenter. The partner's tenant has only Microsoft Entra ID Free and no Global Secure Access licences. The partners already exist as B2B guests in Fabrikam's tenant.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements describe a valid Global Secure Access design? Select TWO.
options: Partners sign in to the GSA client with home accounts and switch to Fabrikam's tenant for assigned apps
Fabrikam's Conditional Access and MFA settings apply to the partners when using its Private Access apps
The partner tenant must buy Microsoft Entra Private Access for each engineer
The partners' devices must be joined to Fabrikam's Microsoft Entra tenant
The partners keep their home tenant's Internet Access tunnel active while connected to Fabrikam
questions.explain: B2B guest access lets guests switch to the resource tenant in the client, and the resource tenant's policies apply. The home tenant needs no GSA licence, device join to the resource tenant is not required, and home tenant tunnels disconnect while the resource tenant is active.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how Microsoft Entra private network connectors communicate?
options: They require inbound TCP 443 from the internet to each connector
They require a site-to-site IPsec VPN to Azure
They must be installed on every user device
They make outbound connections to the Microsoft service, so no inbound firewall ports are needed
questions.explain: Connectors initiate outbound connections, so the datacenter needs no inbound ports. Inbound 443 is not required, no site-to-site VPN is needed, and users run the Global Secure Access client, not connectors.

questions.stem: You used Quick Access to replace the VPN for all internal IP ranges. A finance database server now needs phishing-resistant MFA for a subset of users, while other resources keep the existing policy. What should you do?
options: Create a per-app Global Secure Access application for the server, with a CA policy using an authentication strength
Add the finance server's IP to Quick Access a second time
Require phishing-resistant MFA for the Quick Access application for everyone
Publish the finance server through Azure Front Door
questions.explain: Per-app applications let a subset of private resources get their own assignments and Conditional Access, such as a phishing-resistant authentication strength. Duplicating Quick Access entries does not separate policy, tightening Quick Access affects everyone, and Front Door publishes web apps to the internet.

questions.case: Woodgrove's remote staff use a full-tunnel VPN that gives access to the entire corporate network. Last year an attacker with stolen VPN credentials scanned the network and moved laterally to file servers. The CISO wants per-application access to RDP, SMB and internal web apps, with MFA and device compliance checked per app, and no inbound ports opened in the datacenter.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
