options: Keep the VPN and add an NSG on the VPN gateway subnet
Microsoft Entra Private Access with private network connectors and Conditional Access per application
Microsoft Entra Internet Access with web content filtering
Publish all internal servers with public IPs behind Azure DDoS Protection
questions.explain: Private Access is ZTNA: per-app access for TCP/UDP apps, Conditional Access per app, and outbound-only connectors. NSGs on a VPN gateway do not stop lateral movement, Internet Access filters internet traffic, and public IPs increase exposure.

questions.stem: Which TWO licensing options let users use both Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access? Select TWO.
options: Microsoft Entra Suite plus Microsoft Entra ID P1
Standalone Internet Access and standalone Private Access licences plus Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft Entra ID P1 alone
Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explain: Internet Access and Private Access are both in the Microsoft Entra Suite or sold standalone, and users also need Entra ID P1 or P2. P1 alone includes only the Microsoft traffic profile, Entra ID Free does not include them, and Defender for Cloud Apps is a separate CASB.

questions.stem: Your CISO wants one posture metric covering identity, email, collaboration and device hardening across Microsoft 365. Which tool should you use?
options: Microsoft Secure Score in the Microsoft Defender portal
Secure score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Compliance score in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Azure Advisor score
questions.explain: Microsoft Secure Score measures Microsoft 365, identity, endpoint and connected SaaS posture. The Defender for Cloud secure score measures Azure and multicloud resources. Compliance score measures progress on regulatory controls. Advisor score covers Azure best practice in general.

questions.stem: You are reviewing how Microsoft Secure Score is calculated. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An action already covered by a non-Microsoft product can be set to 'Resolved through alternative mitigation' and still earn points.
Some recommended actions award partial points based on the percentage of users or devices configured.
Microsoft Secure Score is calculated from Azure subscription resources such as virtual machines and storage accounts.

questions.explain: Alternative mitigation earns points, and actions such as MFA coverage are scored proportionally. Azure resource posture belongs to the Defender for Cloud secure score, not Microsoft Secure Score.

questions.case: Fabrikam's board asks for quarterly evidence that Microsoft 365 hardening is improving, and how Fabrikam compares with peers. The security team already uses a third-party identity provider that enforces MFA, which Secure Score currently reports as not addressed. The board also wants the decision on legacy mailbox auditing recorded.
questions.stem: Which approach best meets the board's needs?
options: Export Compliance Manager improvement actions monthly and compare them with industry templates
Track Secure Score history and peer comparison, and set MFA to Resolved through alternative mitigation
Use the Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard with the MCSB standard assigned
Use Entra ID Protection risk reports and mark risky users as dismissed
questions.explain: Secure Score provides history, trends and comparison with similar organisations. Marking third-party MFA as alternative mitigation credits it correctly, and a decision can be recorded as Risk accepted. Compliance Manager tracks regulations, Defender for Cloud covers Azure, and ID Protection reports user risk, not posture.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature opens email attachments in a sandbox to detect zero-day malware before delivery?
options: Safe Links
Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)
Safe Attachments
Spoof intelligence
questions.explain: Safe Attachments detonates attachments, and files in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams, in a sandbox. Safe Links checks URLs at time of click. ZAP removes messages after delivery. Spoof intelligence handles sender spoofing in EOP.

questions.stem: You are evaluating whether Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 is enough. Which TWO capabilities require Plan 2? Select TWO.
options: Safe Links in Microsoft Teams
Attack simulation training
User and domain impersonation protection
Automated investigation and response (AIR)
Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams
questions.explain: Attack simulation training and AIR are Plan 2 features, along with Threat Explorer, Threat Trackers and Campaigns. Safe Links, Safe Attachments for SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams, and impersonation protection are all in Plan 1.

questions.case: Tailspin Toys has Microsoft 365 E3, so it has only Exchange Online Protection. Finance staff keep receiving emails impersonating the CEO's name from look-alike domains, and some contain links to credential-harvesting pages. Tailspin has no SOC and wants the lowest-cost licence that adds impersonation protection and time-of-click URL checks.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Tune EOP anti-spam policies and add the look-alike domains to the Tenant Allow/Block List
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps with an anomaly detection policy
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1
questions.explain: Plan 1 adds user and domain impersonation protection and Safe Links, which is exactly what is needed. Plan 2 adds SOC tooling Tailspin can't use. Block lists only react to known domains. Defender for Cloud Apps doesn't filter email.

questions.stem: You need to find which unsanctioned cloud storage and generative AI apps employees use from corporate devices, with a risk rating for each app. Which Defender for Cloud Apps capability should you use?
options: Cloud Discovery
App connectors
Conditional Access app control
App governance
questions.explain: Cloud Discovery analyses traffic (for example through the Defender for Endpoint integration) and rates apps from the cloud app catalog. App connectors need an API connection to a known app. Conditional Access app control proxies sessions. App governance covers OAuth apps.

questions.stem: Contractors on unmanaged laptops must be able to view Salesforce records in a browser but must not download files labelled Confidential. Blocking must happen in real time. What should you design?
options: An Intune app protection policy for the Salesforce web app
A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy using the Salesforce app connector
An Entra Conditional Access policy using Conditional Access App Control, with a session policy
An Endpoint DLP policy in Microsoft Purview targeting the contractors' devices
questions.explain: The session control routes browser sessions through the Defender for Cloud Apps proxy, where a session policy blocks downloads inline. App connector policies act after the fact. Endpoint DLP needs onboarded devices. App protection policies target mobile and managed apps, not this browser session.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Session policies through Conditional Access app control apply to the Microsoft Teams desktop app.
App governance can identify OAuth apps that have overprivileged or unused permissions.
Apps marked Unsanctioned can be blocked on devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

questions.explain: Session controls only work in browser sessions, not desktop clients such as Teams. App governance monitors OAuth app permissions and hygiene. The Defender for Endpoint integration can enforce blocks on unsanctioned apps.

questions.stem: Only Windows devices that meet your Intune BitLocker and OS version rules may access SharePoint Online. Which Conditional Access grant control enforces this?
options: Require approved client app
Require device to be marked as compliant
Require app protection policy
Require authentication strength
questions.explain: Intune compliance policies evaluate BitLocker and OS version, and Conditional Access enforces the result with 'Require device to be marked as compliant'. App protection and approved client app work at app level. Authentication strength controls the sign-in method.

questions.case: Northwind Health lets clinicians use personal iOS and Android phones for Outlook and Teams. Staff refuse to enrol personal devices. Compliance requires that patient data in these apps is encrypted, can't be copied into personal apps, and can be removed when a clinician leaves, without touching personal photos or apps.
questions.stem: Which design meets the requirements?
options: Intune compliance policies with Conditional Access 'Require device to be marked as compliant'
Windows Autopilot with device configuration profiles
Defender for Cloud Apps session policies for Outlook and Teams mobile apps
Intune app protection policies with Conditional Access 'Require app protection policy'
questions.explain: App protection policies work without enrolment, encrypt corporate data, restrict copy/paste and support selective wipe. Compliance policies need enrolment. Autopilot is for Windows provisioning. Defender for Cloud Apps session controls don't apply to native mobile apps.

questions.stem: You are evaluating the integration between Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Which TWO capabilities does it provide? Select TWO.
options: A compliance policy can require devices to be at or under a specified machine risk score
Safe Links is applied automatically to browsers on enrolled devices
Devices can be onboarded to Defender for Endpoint through an Intune endpoint security EDR policy
Conditional Access is no longer needed to block non-compliant devices
Purview Endpoint DLP is replaced by Intune configuration profiles
questions.explain: Intune can onboard devices to Defender for Endpoint through EDR policies and use the MDE machine risk score in compliance. Conditional Access still enforces compliance. Safe Links is Defender for Office 365. Endpoint DLP stays a Purview capability.

questions.stem: You apply a sensitivity label with container settings to a private Microsoft Teams team. What does this label control?
options: The label applied to every existing document in the team's SharePoint site
Retention and deletion of chat messages in the team
Encryption of all files uploaded to the team
Privacy, guest access and external sharing for the team and its site
questions.explain: Container labels govern the team, group or site: privacy, guest access, external sharing and unmanaged-device access. They don't label or encrypt the files inside. Retention is handled by retention policies.

questions.stem: You are designing a rollout that automatically labels existing confidential files in SharePoint Online. Put the steps in order.
options: Define the label taxonomy and encryption settings with the business
Publish the sensitivity labels to users with a label policy
Create a service-side auto-labelling policy and run it in simulation mode
Review the simulation results, then turn the policy on
questions.explain: Labels must exist and be published before auto-labelling can use them. Service-side auto-labelling always starts in simulation, so you can check matches before labels are applied to data at rest.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Purview in Microsoft 365, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Audit (Standard) keeps audit records for 180 days by default.
Service-side auto-labelling can label files at rest in SharePoint Online without a user opening them.
Encryption from a sensitivity label is removed automatically when a file is emailed outside the organisation.

questions.explain: Audit (Standard) retention is 180 days, and Audit (Premium) is one year by default. Service-side policies label data at rest. Label encryption stays with the file wherever it goes; that is the point of persistent protection.

questions.stem: Microsoft 365 Copilot must not use files labelled Highly Confidential in its responses. Users must still open and edit those files normally, and label encryption settings must not change. What should you configure?
options: Restricted Content Discovery on every SharePoint site
A Purview DLP policy for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location with a sensitivity label condition
An Insider Risk Management policy based on the Risky AI usage template
A Communication Compliance policy for Copilot interactions
questions.explain: The DLP Copilot location can stop Copilot processing items with a chosen label, while users keep their access. RCD works per site, not per label. Insider Risk and Communication Compliance detect behaviour but don't stop Copilot using content.

questions.case: Contoso starts a Microsoft 365 Copilot pilot next week. A DSPM data risk assessment shows 25 SharePoint sites with HR and legal content shared with 'Everyone except external users'. Fixing the permissions with site owners will take two months. Until then, leadership wants that content kept out of Copilot answers, and users' existing access must not change.
questions.stem: What should you implement first?
options: Apply Restricted Content Discovery to the 25 sites
Apply restricted access control to the 25 sites
Apply a retention policy that deletes content older than one year on the sites
Remove Copilot licences from users who have access to the sites
questions.explain: Restricted Content Discovery hides sites from Copilot and org-wide search without changing permissions, so it is the right interim measure. Restricted access control changes who can access the site. Retention deletes data. Removing licences defeats the pilot.

questions.stem: You are designing Purview controls for Microsoft 365 Copilot. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A single DLP policy can include both the Microsoft 365 Copilot location and the Exchange email location.
In a Copilot location rule, sensitive information type and sensitivity label conditions must be in separate rules.
For encrypted content, the user needs the EXTRACT and VIEW usage rights for Copilot to use it.

questions.explain: Choosing the Copilot location (Custom template) disables the other locations, so it needs its own policy. SIT and label conditions can't share a rule. Copilot honours Rights Management, so EXTRACT and VIEW are required.

questions.stem: You must assess the security posture of 150 apps on App Service and AKS, including findings from their GitHub and Azure DevOps repositories. Which solution should you use?
options: Microsoft Secure Score
Azure Advisor cost recommendations
Microsoft Defender for Cloud with DevOps security connectors
Microsoft Purview Data Map
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud assesses Azure workloads against MCSB, and its DevOps security connectors bring in code, secret, dependency and IaC findings. Secure Score covers Microsoft 365. Advisor cost recommendations aren't security. Purview Data Map catalogues data, not app posture.

questions.stem: You are building a prioritised remediation backlog for an Azure application portfolio. Which TWO actions give the most useful prioritisation data? Select TWO.
options: Use Defender CSPM attack path analysis to find internet-exposed workloads that can reach sensitive data
Enable Intune compliance policies for the App Service plans
Turn on Safe Links for developer mailboxes
Tag each app with its business criticality and data classification
Deploy Insider Risk Management to the AKS clusters
questions.explain: Attack paths show exploitable exposure, and criticality and classification tags show impact. Together they rank risk. Intune doesn't manage App Service, Safe Links protects email, and Insider Risk Management doesn't assess cluster posture.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank's Defender for Cloud shows 3,400 open recommendations across 200 apps. The team can fix about 150 a month. Some apps are internal reporting tools, and others are internet-facing payment and customer apps that process cardholder data. Leadership asks how to sequence the work.
questions.stem: Which prioritisation approach should you recommend?
options: Fix recommendations in alphabetical order by resource group to ensure full coverage
Start with internet-facing apps that process sensitive data, ranked by attack paths and severity
Fix the recommendations with the highest secure score impact first, whatever the app
Fix internal reporting tools first because they are smaller and quicker
questions.explain: Risk combines exposure, data sensitivity, criticality and exploitability, and attack paths make that concrete. Score impact alone ignores business context. Alphabetical order or quick wins on low-risk apps leave the most dangerous exposure open the longest.

questions.stem: In a threat model, a customer could plausibly deny authorising a funds transfer because the app keeps no reliable record. Which STRIDE category is this?
options: Spoofing
Tampering
Elevation of privilege
Repudiation
questions.explain: Repudiation is the ability to deny an action because there is no trustworthy evidence. The mitigation is audit logs and tamper-evident records. Spoofing is impersonation, tampering is unauthorised change, and elevation is gaining extra privileges.

questions.stem: You use the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool for a new claims app. Which artefact must you create so the tool can generate candidate threats?
options: A data flow diagram showing processes, data stores, flows and trust boundaries
A list of Azure Policy assignments for the subscription
A Bicep template of the target infrastructure
A CVSS score for each known CVE in the app's dependencies
questions.explain: The tool generates STRIDE threats from a data flow diagram, especially where flows cross trust boundaries. Bicep templates and policy assignments are inputs for IaC scanning. CVSS scores belong to vulnerability management, not design-time threat modelling.

questions.stem: Which TWO pairs correctly match a STRIDE threat category with its primary mitigation? Select TWO.
options: Repudiation: encryption at rest
Spoofing: strong authentication such as MFA or managed identities
Denial of service: sensitivity labels
Elevation of privilege: least-privilege authorisation such as scoped RBAC
Tampering: rate limiting
questions.explain: Spoofing breaks authentication, and elevation of privilege breaks authorisation. Repudiation needs auditing, denial of service needs availability controls such as rate limits and DDoS Protection, and tampering needs integrity controls such as signing and hashing.

questions.stem: Put the steps of Microsoft's threat modeling process in order.
options: Define security requirements
Create an application diagram
Identify threats
Mitigate threats
Validate that threats have been mitigated
questions.explain: Microsoft's five-step process starts with requirements and a diagram. Threats are found from the diagram (for example with STRIDE), then mitigated, and the mitigations are checked. Repeat whenever the design changes.

questions.stem: In a DevSecOps strategy, what does 'shift left' mean?
options: Moving workloads from IaaS to PaaS to reduce the security burden
Moving security checks earlier in the development lifecycle, where fixes cost less
Moving SOC monitoring to an outsourced provider
Moving deployments to a canary ring before production
questions.explain: Shift left means finding security issues early, through threat modelling, IDE checks, secret scanning and SAST, rather than after release. Canary rings are a release practice, PaaS moves responsibility to the provider, and SOC outsourcing is about operations.

questions.stem: You are placing security controls along a CI/CD lifecycle for a containerised app. Put the controls in the order they occur.
options: Secret scanning with push protection blocks a commit that contains a key
SAST and dependency scanning run on the pull request
IaC templates and the container image are scanned in the build
Azure Policy and approvals gate the release to production
Defender for Cloud monitors the running workload
questions.explain: Push protection acts at commit time, SAST and SCA run at PR review, artefact scans run in the build, policy gates control release, and runtime protection covers operations. Each stage catches what earlier ones missed.

questions.stem: For each statement about application security testing, select Yes if true.

statements.s: DAST analyses source code without running the application.
Software composition analysis identifies known-vulnerable open-source dependencies.
A full-lifecycle strategy still needs runtime protection even when shift-left testing is mature.

questions.explain: DAST tests a running app; source analysis is SAST. SCA finds vulnerable packages. Shift left reduces defects but can't stop zero-days or misconfiguration in production, so WAF, Defender for Cloud and monitoring are still needed.

questions.case: A popular npm package used by Litware's customer portal was hijacked and published a malicious version, which Litware's build pulled automatically. Litware builds in Azure Pipelines and wants to reduce its software supply chain risk without blocking developers from using open source.
questions.stem: Which design change best addresses the root cause?
options: Turn on Azure WAF Prevention mode in front of the portal
Enable Defender for Storage malware scanning on the build artefact storage account
Run DAST weekly against the production portal
Use an internal Azure Artifacts feed with upstream sources, pinned versions and dependency scanning in the pipeline
questions.explain: A controlled feed with pinned versions and SCA stops unvetted versions reaching builds and flags known-bad packages. WAF and DAST act at runtime, after the malicious code has shipped. Storage malware scanning isn't designed to catch malicious package logic.

questions.stem: You need a detailed, testable set of security requirements to use as acceptance criteria for customer-facing web apps. Which OWASP project should you adopt?
options: OWASP Top 10
OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)
OWASP Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)
OWASP ZAP
questions.explain: ASVS gives testable requirements at three verification levels. The Top 10 is an awareness list, SAMM measures programme maturity, and ZAP is a DAST tool.

questions.stem: You are writing mandatory secure coding standards for Azure-hosted apps. Which TWO practices should be included? Select TWO.
options: Retrieve secrets from Azure Key Vault using the app's managed identity
Use APIM subscription keys as the only authentication for partner APIs
Use parameterised queries for all database access
Allow TLS 1.0 for internal services to simplify testing
Write a custom encryption routine for each app to avoid shared weaknesses
questions.explain: Key Vault plus managed identity removes secrets from code, and parameterised queries prevent injection. Subscription keys aren't strong authentication, TLS 1.0 is obsolete, and custom cryptography goes against SDL guidance to use approved, standard libraries.

questions.stem: Developers have accidentally committed storage account keys to GitHub several times. You must stop secrets reaching the repository in the first place. Which control should you require?
options: Dependabot alerts
CodeQL code scanning on pull requests
Branch protection rules that require two reviewers
Secret scanning with push protection
questions.explain: Push protection blocks a push that contains a detected secret, so it never lands in history. Dependabot covers dependencies, CodeQL finds code vulnerabilities, and branch protection reviews changes after they are pushed to a branch.

questions.stem: You are mapping application security requirements to Microsoft technologies. For each mapping, select Yes if it is appropriate.

statements.s: Detect anomalous calls and unauthenticated endpoints for APIs published in API Management: Microsoft Defender for APIs.
Let consumers sign up and sign in to a public app with social accounts: Microsoft Entra External ID.
Classify and label documents uploaded to a SharePoint site: Azure Web Application Firewall.

questions.explain: Defender for APIs protects APIs published in APIM, and External ID is Microsoft's customer identity platform. Document classification is done with Purview sensitivity labels and auto-labelling. A WAF inspects HTTP traffic, not document content.

questions.case: Adatum is building a three-tier web app on App Service with Azure SQL. Requirements: the app tier must reach Azure SQL with no stored credentials; Azure SQL must not be reachable from the internet; and every database connection must be attributable to an Entra identity.
questions.stem: Which combination meets all three requirements?
options: A managed identity for the App Service, a private endpoint for Azure SQL, and Entra-only authentication
A SQL login in Key Vault, Azure SQL firewall rules for App Service outbound IPs, and SQL auditing
A service principal with a client secret in app settings, service endpoints, and TDE
Shared access signatures, an Application Gateway WAF in front of Azure SQL, and dynamic data masking
questions.explain: A managed identity removes credentials, a private endpoint removes internet reachability, and Entra-only authentication makes every connection an Entra identity. SQL logins and client secrets are still stored credentials, and a WAF doesn't front SQL traffic.

questions.stem: A public web app must be protected against both large network-layer floods and application-layer attacks such as SQL injection. Which TWO services should you include? Select TWO.
options: Azure Bastion
Azure DDoS Protection
Microsoft Defender for Storage
Azure Web Application Firewall
Azure Private DNS zones
questions.explain: DDoS Protection mitigates volumetric L3/L4 attacks, and Azure WAF inspects L7 requests for OWASP attacks. They complement each other. Bastion is for VM admin access, Defender for Storage protects storage accounts, and private DNS handles name resolution.

questions.stem: Twenty VM scale set instances and three Function apps must share one identity, which must be pre-granted RBAC access and survive when any single resource is deleted. Which identity type should you use?
options: A system-assigned managed identity on each resource
An app registration with a client secret
A user-assigned managed identity
A Microsoft Entra B2B guest account
questions.explain: A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone resource that can be attached to many resources and has its own lifecycle. System-assigned identities are 1:1 and deleted with the resource. Client secrets must be stored and rotated. Guest accounts are for people.

questions.stem: A GitHub Actions workflow must authenticate to Azure with no stored secret, and only when it runs in the repo's 'prod' environment. Complete the federated identity credential.
options: "repo:contoso/payments:environment:prod"
"repo:contoso/*:environment:prod"
"https://github.com/contoso/payments"
"api://AzureADTokenExchange/prod"
questions.explain: The subject must exactly match the GitHub token's sub claim, which for environments is repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:<name>. Wildcards aren't supported in standard federated credentials. A repo URL or an audience value isn't a valid subject.

questions.case: Proseware runs a single-tenant daemon app (an app registration with a certificate) that calls Microsoft Graph and Azure Resource Manager. Security wants token requests from this service principal blocked if they come from outside the company's egress IP ranges, or if Entra ID Protection marks the service principal as high risk.
questions.stem: What should you design?
options: Conditional Access requiring MFA for the service principal, with named locations
Conditional Access for workload identities with location and service principal risk conditions, licensed with Workload Identities Premium
Azure Policy denying role assignments to the service principal from untrusted networks
Convert the app to a system-assigned managed identity and apply Conditional Access to it
questions.explain: Conditional Access for workload identities covers single-tenant service principals, with location and service principal risk conditions and Block as the grant. It needs Workload Identities Premium. MFA can't apply to workloads, managed identities aren't supported, and Azure Policy doesn't evaluate sign-ins.

questions.stem: In Azure API Management, you must reject any call that lacks a valid Microsoft Entra access token for the API's audience. Complete the inbound policy element.
questions.code:
<inbound>
  <base />
  <____ header-name="Authorization" failed-validation-httpcode="401">
    <openid-config url="https://login.microsoftonline.com/contoso.onmicrosoft.com/.well-known/openid-configuration" />
    <audiences>
      <audience>api://orders</audience>
    </audiences>
  </validate-jwt>
</inbound>
options: check-header
validate-jwt
authentication-managed-identity
validate-client-certificate
questions.explain: validate-jwt checks the token signature through the OpenID configuration, plus the audience and claims, and returns 401 on failure. check-header only checks that a header exists. authentication-managed-identity gets a token for the back end. validate-client-certificate is for mTLS.

questions.stem: Each client IP may call a public API published in API Management at most 20 times every 60 seconds. Complete the policy.
questions.code:
<inbound>
  <base />
  <rate-limit-by-key calls="20" renewal-period="60"
     ____="@(context.Request.IpAddress)" />
</inbound>
options: counter-key
increment-condition
remaining-calls-header-name
retry-after-header-name
questions.explain: counter-key is the required attribute that sets what the limit is tracked by, here the caller IP. increment-condition decides which calls count, and the header-name attributes only add response headers.

questions.case: Relecloud exposes internal microservice APIs to partners over the internet. Requirements: inspect traffic for OWASP attacks before it reaches the gateway; the API gateway must not have a public endpoint; back-end services must accept only gateway traffic with no stored credentials; and the team wants API inventory with alerts for unauthenticated endpoints.
questions.stem: Which architecture should you recommend?
options: Front Door Standard with custom WAF rules, APIM in external mode, back ends using subscription keys
Azure Firewall Premium with IDPS in front of APIM in external mode, and back ends using client secrets
Application Gateway WAF v2, then APIM in internal VNet mode using managed identity to back ends, plus Defender for APIs
APIM with a public IP and ip-filter, back ends with SQL logins, and Defender for App Service
questions.explain: Application Gateway WAF in front of internal-mode APIM gives L7 inspection with no public gateway. Managed identity authenticates to back ends without secrets, and Defender for APIs provides inventory and unauthenticated-endpoint findings. The other options leave public gateways or stored credentials.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure API Management security, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A subscription key alone gives strong proof of the calling user's identity.
Defender for APIs currently protects APIs published in Azure API Management.
Named values in API Management can reference secrets stored in Azure Key Vault.

questions.explain: Subscription keys are shared secrets for identifying and metering callers, not strong authentication, so pair them with OAuth token validation. Defender for APIs onboards APIs from APIM. Key Vault-backed named values keep secrets out of policies.

questions.stem: A multi-region web app needs managed OWASP rules, bot protection and Private Link to its origins, enforced at Microsoft's global edge. Which option should you choose?
options: Azure Front Door Standard with a WAF policy
Application Gateway WAF v2 in each region
Azure Firewall Premium
Azure Front Door Premium with a WAF policy
questions.explain: Front Door Premium adds the Microsoft-managed rule set, bot protection and Private Link origins at the global edge. Front Door Standard supports only custom WAF rules. Application Gateway is regional, and Azure Firewall isn't a web application firewall for HTTP apps.

questions.stem: A WAF policy uses DRS 2.2 in Prevention mode with the default anomaly threshold. A request matches one Warning-severity rule and nothing else. What happens?
options: The request is allowed because its anomaly score of 3 is below the threshold of 5
The request is blocked because every match blocks in Prevention mode
The request is redirected to a CAPTCHA challenge
The request is logged only, because DRS 2.2 doesn't support Prevention mode
questions.explain: DRS 2.x uses anomaly scoring. Warning adds 3, and the action fires at 5 or more, so a single Warning match passes while one Critical (5) blocks. Per-rule blocking was the older pre-2.0 behaviour. Prevention mode is supported.

questions.stem: You are introducing Azure WAF in front of an existing production app with minimal disruption. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a WAF policy with the latest Default Rule Set in Detection mode
Associate the policy with the Front Door endpoint or Application Gateway
Analyse WAF logs for false positives on legitimate traffic
Add targeted exclusions or rule overrides for the false positives
Switch the policy to Prevention mode
questions.explain: Detection mode logs matches without blocking, so you can find and tune false positives with exclusions before blocking. Turning on Prevention first risks blocking real users.

questions.case: Fourth Coffee hosts three apps on one Application Gateway WAF v2: a public shop, a partner portal, and an internal HR site on the same gateway. The partner portal's legacy SOAP endpoint at /legacy/* triggers many SQL injection false positives. Security won't weaken protection for the shop or the rest of the portal.
questions.stem: What is the best design?
options: Switch the global WAF policy to Detection mode
Disable the SQL injection rule group in the global WAF policy
Move all three apps to Front Door Standard with custom rules only
Associate a per-URI WAF policy with tuned exclusions for /legacy/*
questions.explain: Application Gateway WAF v2 supports global, per-site and per-URI policies, so tuning can be limited to /legacy/*. Detection mode or disabling the rule group globally weakens every app. Front Door Standard has no managed rules at all.

questions.stem: You need to stop credential-stuffing bursts against /login on a Front Door-hosted app, and block traffic from countries where the company doesn't operate. Which TWO WAF features should you use? Select TWO.
options: A rate-limit custom rule matching the /login path
A geo-filtering custom rule
DRS paranoia level 2 rules
Defender for Storage malware scanning
An Azure Firewall DNAT rule
questions.explain: Rate-limit custom rules cap requests per client to a path, and geo-filter custom rules allow or block by country. Higher paranoia rules increase injection detection, not rate control. Defender for Storage and Azure Firewall DNAT don't apply here.

questions.stem: You need to detect real customer account numbers with very few false positives by matching against values in your CRM database. Which classification method should you use?
options: A trainable classifier
Exact data match (EDM) sensitive information type
A keyword dictionary
A regular-expression sensitive information type
questions.explain: EDM matches content against hashed values uploaded from your own data source, which gives very precise detection. Regex SITs match any number with the right pattern, keyword dictionaries match words, and trainable classifiers recognise document types rather than specific values.

questions.case: A retailer must prove to PCI assessors where cardholder data lives across Azure SQL, ADLS Gen2, on-premises SQL Server and Amazon S3, with a searchable inventory and lineage. Separately, the cloud security team wants to know which internet-exposed workloads can reach those stores.
questions.stem: Which pair of solutions should you recommend?
options: Defender for Cloud sensitive data discovery for the inventory, and Microsoft Secure Score for exposure
Purview Information Protection content explorer for the inventory, and Defender for Storage for exposure
Microsoft Purview Data Map scans for the inventory, and Defender CSPM attack paths for exposure
Azure SQL Data Discovery & Classification for the inventory, and Azure Advisor for exposure
questions.explain: Purview Data Map scans multicloud and on-premises sources into a catalogue with classifications and lineage. Defender CSPM attack paths show exposed workloads that can reach sensitive stores. Defender's sensitive data discovery samples rather than fully cataloguing, content explorer covers M365, and SQL classification covers SQL only.

questions.stem: For each statement about data discovery and classification, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Defender for Cloud sensitive data discovery uses the same Purview sensitive information types and can import custom ones.
Defender for Cloud sensitive data discovery reads every row in every database table.
Trainable classifiers can identify content such as contracts that has no fixed pattern.

questions.explain: Defender for Cloud uses Purview's classification engine and SITs, including custom ones. It samples rows and files rather than doing full scans. Trainable classifiers use machine learning to recognise categories of content.

questions.stem: Threat analysis shows the top risk to a claims data platform is an attacker using stolen but valid Entra credentials to download data. Which control most directly reduces this risk?
options: Enable infrastructure encryption on the storage accounts
Rotate TDE protectors in Key Vault every 90 days
Enable TLS 1.3 on all endpoints
Enforce least-privilege data roles with PIM and Conditional Access, and alert on anomalous access with Defender
questions.explain: Valid credentials are decrypted transparently, so encryption at rest, key rotation and TLS don't stop this attack. Limiting who has data access, requiring strong sign-in conditions and detecting unusual extraction all address credential misuse.

questions.case: A regional bank ranks ransomware destroying its core banking data and backups as its top data threat. Second is exfiltration of customer PII from Azure Storage over public endpoints. Third is staff emailing statements to personal accounts. The budget covers one large project this quarter and smaller changes later.
questions.stem: Which project should be prioritised first?
options: Immutable Azure Backup vaults with soft delete and multi-user authorisation, plus blob versioning and immutability for critical data
Purview DLP policies for Exchange Online
Private endpoints for all storage accounts
Insider Risk Management with Adaptive Protection
questions.explain: The top-ranked threat is ransomware destroying data and backups. Immutable, soft-deleted backups protected by multi-user authorisation make recovery possible. Private endpoints address the second threat and DLP the third, so they come later in the plan.

questions.stem: You must reduce the risk of data exfiltration from Azure Storage and Azure SQL by external attackers. Which THREE controls remove access paths rather than only detecting misuse? Select THREE.
options: Disable public network access and use private endpoints
Disallow Shared Key authorisation and use Entra ID RBAC
Enable Microsoft Entra-only authentication for Azure SQL
Enable Defender for Storage activity monitoring
Stream SQL audit logs to Microsoft Sentinel
questions.explain: Private endpoints, removing shared keys and Entra-only SQL authentication all take away whole attack paths. Defender activity monitoring and Sentinel auditing are valuable, but they detect misuse rather than prevent it.

questions.stem: Regulation requires encryption keys in a single-tenant, FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSM pool that only your organisation controls. Which service should you select?
options: Azure Key Vault Standard
Azure Key Vault Premium
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
Microsoft-managed keys with infrastructure encryption
questions.explain: Managed HSM gives a dedicated single-tenant HSM pool that you control through its security domain. Key Vault Premium uses HSM-backed keys in multitenant HSMs, and Standard is software-protected. Microsoft-managed keys aren't customer-controlled.

questions.stem: For each statement about encryption in Azure, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Infrastructure encryption can be enabled on an existing storage account at any time.
A key vault used for Azure Storage customer-managed keys must have soft delete and purge protection enabled.
Once purge protection is enabled on a key vault, it can't be disabled.

questions.explain: Infrastructure encryption must be chosen at account creation. Storage CMK requires soft delete and purge protection on the vault. Purge protection is irreversible, which stops a malicious admin destroying keys early.

questions.stem: A key vault holds customer-managed keys for SQL TDE. You must make sure deleted keys can't be permanently purged before the retention period ends. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code:
az keyvault update \
  --name kv-prod-tde \
  --resource-group rg-security \
  ____ true
options: --enable-soft-delete
--enable-rbac-authorization
--enable-purge-protection
--enabled-for-disk-encryption
questions.explain: --enable-purge-protection blocks permanent deletion until retention expires, and it can't be turned off later. Soft delete is already always on. RBAC authorisation changes the permission model, and enabled-for-disk-encryption lets Azure Disk Encryption read secrets.

questions.case: Lamna Healthcare runs 300 Windows and Linux VMs protected by Azure Disk Encryption. An auditor notes that ADE is being retired and asks for a target design that also encrypts temp disks and caches, and lets Lamna use its own keys in Key Vault.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Keep ADE and enable infrastructure encryption on the VMs' storage accounts
Redeploy the VMs with encryption at host enabled, using a disk encryption set with a customer-managed key
Convert ADE to encryption at host in place on the existing disks
Enable TDE inside each VM's operating system
questions.explain: Encryption at host is the ADE replacement. It encrypts temp disks, caches and data flows, and works with a disk encryption set for CMK. In-place conversion isn't supported, so new disks and VMs are needed. Managed disks don't use customer storage accounts, and TDE is a SQL feature.

questions.stem: An internal RAG chatbot indexes documents from many departments into Azure AI Search. Users report the bot quotes documents they can't open in SharePoint. What should you design?
options: Enable customer-managed keys on the AI Search service
Enable Prompt Shields on the model deployment
Move the AI Search service behind a private endpoint
Apply document-level security filters (security trimming) on the index based on users' groups
questions.explain: An index doesn't carry source permissions by default, so retrieval must be trimmed to what each user may access. CMK and private endpoints protect the service, not per-user access. Prompt Shields detect jailbreak and injection attempts, not authorisation gaps.

questions.case: Contoso is launching a customer-facing generative AI assistant on Microsoft Foundry, grounded in product and order data. The security architect must address jailbreak attempts, alerting the SOC to AI-specific threats such as data leakage, and stopping employees pasting customer PII into consumer AI websites from their Windows laptops.
questions.stem: Which THREE components should the design include? Select THREE.
options: Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields
Microsoft Defender for AI Services
Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP for generative AI websites
Defender for Office 365 Safe Links
Azure Disk Encryption on the model hosts
questions.explain: Prompt Shields detect jailbreak and prompt injection. Defender for AI Services alerts on AI threats such as data leakage and jailbreak. Endpoint DLP can block pasting sensitive data into third-party AI sites. Safe Links protects URLs, and ADE is irrelevant to managed AI services and is being retired.

questions.stem: For each statement about securing data in AI workloads, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Apps calling Azure OpenAI in Foundry should use managed identities with Azure RBAC rather than API keys where possible.
Defender for AI Services scans image and audio tokens as well as text.
Microsoft Purview audit can capture prompts and responses from supported AI apps.

questions.explain: Managed identities remove keys from AI apps. Defender for AI Services threat protection scans text tokens only. Purview captures AI interactions, including referenced files and labels, in the unified audit log.

questions.stem: National ID numbers in an Azure SQL database must be unreadable to DBAs and cloud operators, while the payroll app can still look up employees by ID. What should you use?
options: Always Encrypted with deterministic encryption on the column
Transparent data encryption with a customer-managed key
Dynamic data masking on the column
Row-level security
questions.explain: Always Encrypted encrypts on the client, so the engine and DBAs only see ciphertext, and deterministic encryption allows equality lookups. TDE is transparent to anyone who can query. Masking can be bypassed by privileged users, and row-level security filters rows, not column values.

questions.stem: Security requires that the logical server hosting Azure SQL Database accepts only Microsoft Entra identities and no SQL logins. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code:
az sql server ____ enable \
  --resource-group rg-data \
  --name sql-payroll-prod
options: ad-admin
ad-only-auth
tde-key
audit-policy
questions.explain: az sql server ad-only-auth enable turns on Microsoft Entra-only authentication, which disables SQL authentication. ad-admin sets the Entra admin but leaves SQL logins working. tde-key manages the TDE protector, and audit-policy configures auditing.

questions.case: A financial services firm is building an Azure Synapse Analytics workspace for regulated trading data. Auditors require that Spark and pipelines can't write data to storage accounts outside the firm's own Entra tenant. The project manager suggests creating the workspace now with default settings and adding restrictions after the pilot.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Create the workspace now, then enable data exfiltration protection after the pilot
Use Synapse workspace IP firewall rules to block outbound traffic
Create the workspace with a managed virtual network and data exfiltration protection, and allow only approved Entra tenants
Rely on Defender for Storage to alert on writes to external accounts
questions.explain: Data exfiltration protection limits egress to managed private endpoints in approved tenants, and it can only be set at workspace creation. Adding it later isn't possible. Workspace firewall rules control inbound access, and Defender for Storage detects rather than prevents.

questions.stem: A trading ledger in Azure SQL Database must let auditors detect any tampering with historical rows, even by DBAs, with digests kept outside the database. Which TWO elements should the design include? Select TWO.
options: Ledger tables in the database
Dynamic data masking on all columns
Automatic digest storage in Azure Confidential Ledger or immutable Blob Storage
TDE with a service-managed key
A read-scale replica
questions.explain: Ledger tables hash every change, and digests kept in Azure Confidential Ledger or immutable blobs let verification detect tampering. Masking, TDE and read replicas don't provide tamper evidence.

questions.stem: After leaked account keys, you must force all clients of an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account to authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID only. Complete the command.
questions.code:
az resource update \
  --resource-group rg-orders \
  --name cosmos-orders \
  --resource-type "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts" \
  --set properties.____=true
options: disableKeyBasedMetadataWriteAccess
publicNetworkAccess
enableAutomaticFailover
disableLocalAuth
questions.explain: disableLocalAuth=true blocks primary and secondary key authentication, so clients must use Entra ID with data-plane RBAC. disableKeyBasedMetadataWriteAccess only stops keys changing resources, publicNetworkAccess takes Enabled/Disabled, and automatic failover is about availability.

questions.stem: An App Service app's managed identity must read and write items in an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL container where key-based auth is disabled. What should you assign?
options: The Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor role through a Cosmos DB native SQL role assignment
The Azure RBAC Cosmos DB Operator role on the account
The Azure RBAC Contributor role on the resource group
The DocumentDB Account Contributor role on the subscription
questions.explain: Data-plane access in Cosmos DB for NoSQL uses native role definitions and assignments, such as Built-in Data Contributor. Cosmos DB Operator, Contributor and DocumentDB Account Contributor are Azure RBAC control-plane roles and don't grant item access.

questions.stem: You want SOC alerts for anomalous access and possible SQL injection against an Azure Cosmos DB account. Which Defender for Cloud plan should you enable?
options: Defender for Storage
Defender for Azure Cosmos DB
Defender CSPM
Defender for App Service
questions.explain: Defender for Azure Cosmos DB, one of the Defender for Databases plans, detects anomalous access, SQL injection patterns and suspicious key extraction. Defender for Storage covers storage accounts, Defender CSPM is posture, and Defender for App Service protects web apps.

questions.stem: You must block account keys, account SAS and service SAS on a storage account while still allowing Entra ID access and user delegation SAS. Complete the command.
questions.code:
az storage account update \
  --name stclaimsprod \
  --resource-group rg-claims \
  ____ false
options: --allow-blob-public-access
--https-only
--allow-shared-key-access
--default-action
questions.explain: Setting --allow-shared-key-access to false rejects Shared Key, which also disables account and service SAS. User delegation SAS is signed with Entra credentials, so it still works. The other flags control anonymous access, HTTPS and the network firewall.

questions.case: A broker-dealer must keep trade confirmations in Blob Storage for seven years in non-erasable, non-rewritable form, meeting SEC 17a-4(f). Even storage account owners must not be able to shorten the retention period. Some records also face litigation with no known end date.
questions.stem: Which configuration should you recommend?
options: A locked time-based retention policy, plus legal holds for litigated records
An unlocked time-based retention policy, plus blob soft delete
Blob versioning with a lifecycle management rule that moves blobs to the archive tier
A CanNotDelete resource lock on the storage account, plus a legal hold
questions.explain: A locked time-based policy can only be extended, which meets SEC 17a-4(f), and legal holds keep data until they are cleared. Unlocked policies can be shortened or deleted. Lifecycle rules and resource locks don't make blob data immutable.

questions.stem: Put the layers of an Azure Storage data protection design in order, from the outermost access gate to the innermost recovery safeguard.
options: Private endpoint with public network access disabled
Microsoft Entra ID authorisation with Shared Key disallowed
Encryption at rest with a customer-managed key
Soft delete, versioning and immutability policies
questions.explain: Requests first meet the network boundary, then identity authorisation. Data is encrypted at rest under the customer's key, and soft delete, versioning and immutability provide recovery if something gets through.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Defender for Storage, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Activity monitoring requires you to enable storage resource logs first.
Malware scanning results can be sent through Azure Event Grid to trigger automated responses.
Blob index tags written by malware scanning are tamper-resistant, so they can be the only control for gating downstream processing.

questions.explain: Activity monitoring uses platform telemetry without resource logs. Event Grid delivers scan results to Functions, Logic Apps and similar handlers. Index tags can be changed by anyone with write access, so Microsoft warns not to rely on them alone.

questions.case: Datum Insurance runs SQL Server 2019 on-premises, SQL Server on Azure VMs, Azure SQL Database, Azure Database for PostgreSQL and a public claims upload portal that writes to Blob Storage. Datum wants vulnerability assessment and threat alerts for all databases, and malicious uploads removed automatically with no custom code.
questions.stem: Which design meets the requirements?
options: Defender CSPM for all resources, plus Purview Data Map scans of the upload container
Defender for Servers Plan 2 on all machines, plus Event Grid with a custom Function for uploads
Defender for Azure SQL Databases only, plus Defender for Storage activity monitoring
Defender for Databases (Arc for on-prem SQL) plus Defender for Storage malware scanning with auto-remediation
questions.explain: Defender for Databases covers Azure SQL, SQL servers on machines (Azure VMs and Arc-enabled on-premises) and open-source relational databases. On-upload malware scanning's built-in remediation soft-deletes malicious blobs without code. The other options miss databases or need custom code.
